injuries.shortComment: Dicker made both of his field-goal attempts in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Dicker's 23-yard and 30-yard field goals were the only points scored by the Chargers in the team's blowout loss. While the offense could not get going, as has been the theme all season, Dicker remained reliable. The 26-year-old moves to 9-for-11 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts over six regular-season games in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Kolar caught three of six targets for 20 yards during the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Kolar finished fifth on the Chargers in receiving yards, but he was also second on the team in both catches and targets behind KeAndre Lambert-Smith (five catches on nine targets for 32 yards). Kolar has a 6-57-0 receiving line in his two outings since returning from a two-game absence due to a fractured forearm, but he's stuck in an offense that is one of the worst units in the league this season. The Chargers will look to regroup during the Week 7 bye before facing the Rams in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Vidal turned seven carries into 21 yards and caught three of four passes for 19 yards during the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: The Chargers' run offense struggled Sunday, but Vidal was slightly more efficient than Omarion Hampton (18 yards) on the same number of carries. Vidal has seen more rotational offensive snaps over the Chargers' last three games, and over that span he has logged 20 carries for 103 yards and a touchdown and six catches (on nine targets) for 29 yards and a score. His role may continue to expand following the Week 7 bye, with the Chargers' next game taking place in Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Mitchell turned two carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned four kickoffs for 87 yards during Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Week 6 was the lowest usage Mitchell has seen this season, and his 17 snaps on offense were third most among Chargers running backs behind Omarion Hampton (34) and Kimani Vidal (25). Through six regular-season games, Mitchell has turned 35 carries into 139 yards and added 12 catches (on 15 targets) for 52 yards and a score, but it's hard to put much trust into any of the Chargers' skill-position players given the team's poor start to the season. Perhaps the Week 7 bye will help the Chargers right the ship, with their next game taking place in Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Johnston caught one of three targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Johnston needed just one catch to set a season high in receiving yards, but he was tackled at the 1-yard line to keep him without a touchdown this season after consecutive eight-touchdown regular seasons. The Chargers proceeded to back up 11 yards from there and settled for a field goal. Johnston has caught a deep pass in each of the past two games, securing a 44-yard catch in the Week 5 loss to Seattle prior to the 57-yard catch against the Chiefs. The 2023 first-round pick has just eight catches through five appearances heading into LA's Week 7 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Herbert completed 22 of 37 passes for 204 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed five times for 26 yards.
injuries.longComment: Herbert continued to struggle but once again got little help from his teammates. Top wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) exited early, and the Chargers couldn't generate much on the ground, as Herbert led the team in rushing yards. Herbert was held without a touchdown for the first time this season after throwing exactly one touchdown pass in each of the previous five games. The 0-6 Chargers are the first team to six losses this season, as the Titans notched their first win of the season over the Colts on Sunday to improve to 1-5, while the winless Dolphins were on bye. Herbert will be on bye in Week 7 before his next opportunity to snap this season-opening losing streak in a nominal road game against the Rams in Week 8.

injuries.shortComment: Hampton rushed seven times for 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: The Chargers continued to deloy an ineffective backfield rotation, as Hampton got 11 touches compared to 10 for Kimani Vidal and two for Keaton Mitchell. None of the three running backs exceeded 3.0 yards per carry while QB Justin Herbert led the team with 26 rushing yards. Hampton has been trending in the wrong direction, with his rushing yardage dropping with each subsequent game since a 94-yard performance on the ground in Week 2 against the Raiders. He'll look to reverse that trend in Week 8 against the Rams following a Week 7 bye.

injuries.shortComment: McConkey won't return to Sunday's game at Kansas City due to a concussion.
injuries.longComment: McConkey was being evaluated for a possible head injury early in the second quarter before the Chargers quickly ruled him out. This follows a nearly three-week stretch in which he was dealing with a lingering foot issue that didn't allow him to log a snap in Week 4, despite being active. Now that he's subject to the concussion protocol, McConkey's next game action is up in the air.

injuries.shortComment: Henley (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Henley was listed as questionable for Sunday's game due to a knee injury. The linebacker was limited in practice all week due to the injury but has recovered enough to suit up for the Chargers' Sunday divisional contest against the Chiefs.

injuries.shortComment: The Chargers placed Ingold on injured reserve Thursday due to a shoulder injury.
injuries.longComment: Per Noah Furtado of The Athletic, Ingold wasn't included on the Chargers' initial Week 6 injury report Wednesday before being a late addition on account of the shoulder issue. He'll be sidelined for at least the next four games, making him ineligible to play until Week 11 versus the Jets on Nov. 22. The fullback hadn't logged any carries and recorded three receptions for 35 yards on four targets through Los Angeles' first five games.

injuries.shortComment: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Perryman (undisclosed) won't be reinstated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Per Ricardo Sandoval of USA Today, Harbaugh said back on Sept. 1 that he expected Perryman to spend the minimum four games on IR due to his unspecified injury, but the veteran linebacker will now be sidelined for a sixth straight game to begin the campaign. The 33-year-old appeared in 10 games for the Chargers in 2025, logging 47 tackles and three pass breakups.

injuries.shortComment: The calf injury Nacua sustained Thursday is believed to be "more minor than anything else" and "not significant," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.longComment: Nacua left Thursday's practice with the calf issue, and tests performed afterward appear to have indicated that the wideout did not sustain a serious injury. The report notes that Nacua's availability for Week 7 remains uncertain, but the Rams will presumably provide an official update on both his short- and long-term status at some point Friday.

injuries.shortComment: McDuffie (groin) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
injuries.longComment: McDuffie has been sidelined since sustaining a groin injury in Thursday's practice before the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals. The star cornerback appears to be day-to-day with the injury but there is no clear expectation for a Week 7 return against the Raiders.

injuries.shortComment: Landman (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
injuries.longComment: Landman likely sustained his concussion in the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals. The linebacker has enterted the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to upgrade his practice participation with the approval of an independent neurologist before being cleared for game-day activities. If Landman cannot clear the league's protocol by Sunday's game against the Raiders, veteran linebacker Eric Kendricks could be called up to the active roster in his place.

injuries.shortComment: The Rams placed Turner (groin) on injured reserve Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Turner suffered a significant groin injury during the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, and the health issue is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve. The fourth-year pro will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest that Turner can return is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. In his absence, Braden Fiske should move into a starting role on the defensive line opposite Aaron Donald, while Tyler Davis and Larrell Murchison work in rotation.

injuries.shortComment: Curl finished Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Cardinals with eight tackles (three solo).
injuries.longComment: Curl played every single defensive snap for a third consecutive game and the fourth time this season, and he finished Sunday's contest as the Rams' second-leading tackler behind Nate Landman (10). Curl has registered eight combined tackles in back-to-back outings and is up to 30 tackles (18 solo) and two pass defenses through six regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Lake registered seven tackles (six solo) and an interception during the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Lake picked off Jacoby Brissett early in the first quarter on a pass intended for Trey McBride, which the Rams offense converted into a 44-yard field goal six plays later. It was Lake's second interception of the season, which is already a career high for the 2022 sixth-rounder. He's also up to eight pass defenses through six regular-season games, which is tied for second-most in the NFL behind Jacob Parrish (nine).

injuries.shortComment: Mumpfield caught two of three passes for 15 yards during the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Mumpfield was on the field for only five offensive snaps against the Bills in Week 5, but he was more involved against the Cardinals with 27 offensive snaps. That snap count figures to increase for the Rams' next few games, seeing as Davante Adams is facing a six- to 10-week recovery timeline for a ruptured left hamstring that required surgery, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. The Rams will hit the road for Week 7 against the Raiders, whose defense ranks 25th in fantasy points allowed to opposing wide receivers.

injuries.shortComment: The Rams placed Ford (triceps) on injured reserve Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: The move is an expected one, given that Ford suffered a season-ending triceps injury during the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday. The veteran defensive tackle will shift his focus toward rehab and being fully healthy for the 2027 season, which is the final year of his three-year, $27.6 million contract with the Rams.

injuries.shortComment: Ferguson (ankle), who is eligible to come off injured reserve next week, isn't expected to be ready at that time, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: Ferguson, who was placed on injured reserve in advance of Week 4 action, will be eligible to return in Week 8 against the Chargers. However, it appears as though the tight end's return isn't imminent, with Schefter's report suggesting that Ferguson's recovery "will take some time." In his absence, Tyler Higbee profiles as the Rams' main pass-catching TE, with Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen also mixing in.

injuries.shortComment: Adams (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.longComment: As a result, Adams is slated to miss at least four games, although Ian Rapoport of NFL Network previously suggested that the wideout was hoping to return not too long after the Rams' Week 11 bye. In his absence, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwellare candidates to see added looks behind top WR Puka Nacua.

injuries.shortComment: McManus is slated to sign with the Rams, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.longComment: With Blake Grupe having landed on IR, the Rams are bringing McManus in to fill the void at kicker ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders. McManus represents an option for those who had rostered Grupe or are otherwise looking for kicking help ahead of Week 7, when four teams will be on bye.

injuries.shortComment: The NFL reinstated Jackson on Monday after his one-game suspension for punching Bradley Chubb, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
injuries.longComment: The left tackle was initially issued a two-game suspension for unsportsmanlike conduct for striking Bradley Chubb after the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night in Week 5. Jackson appealed the ruling and had the ban cut to one game, which has now been served.

injuries.shortComment: Higbee caught all four of his targets for 22 yards during the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.longComment: Higbee was not targeted by Matthew Stafford until early in the fourth quarter, but the former fumbled the ball on his first catch of the game, which was recovered by the Cardinals defense. Higbee saw three more passes from Stafford in the quarter, and Sunday's effort snapped his three-game streak of 60-plus yards and five-plus catches. However, the Rams are expected to be without Davante Adams (hamstring) until at least after the Week 11 bye, so Higbee could be Stafford's secondary target in the passing game behind Puka Nacua for the next few games. The Rams hit the road for Week 7 on Oct. 25 against the Raiders, whose defense gives up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.

injuries.shortComment: Rams head coach Sean McVay announced Monday that Grupe will miss the remainder of the season after sustaining a torn ACL in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Cardinals, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
injuries.longComment: Los Angeles placed Grupe on injured reserve earlier Monday and likely will work out multiple kickers over the next few days before deciding on a new option prior to Sunday's game against the Raiders. Signed off the Jets' practice squad last week, Grupe converted a 44-yard field goal in the first quarter of Sunday's contest before sustaining the season-ending injury while attempting to make a tackle on the ensuing kickoff return.

injuries.shortComment: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Garrett (knee) won't have his 21-day practice window opened this week, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
injuries.longComment: The Rams haven't indicated that Garrett has experienced any setbacks since undergoing arthroscopic left knee surgery following the team's Week 1 loss to the 49ers in Australia, but he looks like he'll need more time to complete his rehab before getting back on the field for practice. The ongoing absence of Garrett will continue to loom large heading into Sunday's game against the Raiders, especially with one of the Rams' other key pass rushers (defensive tackle Kobie Turner) set to join Garrett on injured reserve after sustaining a groin injury in the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.

injuries.shortComment: Stafford was 25-for-33 passing for 222 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions during Sunday's 18-16 defeat against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Stafford's streak of outings with at least 300 yards passing came to a close at four games, but he offset it with his fourth performance with multiple TD passes through the first six weeks of the season. With the Rams sitting at 2-4 and seeking to right the ship, he does have a get-right game on paper next Sunday in Las Vegas, and he has several talented skill-position players at his disposal, though star wideout Davante Adams exited on the Rams' second-to-last-offensive play of the game Sunday with what may have been a knee injury. However, the team didn't provide any information about Adams' departure or status following the loss, so it's currently very murky as to whether he's in danger of missing any time.

injuries.shortComment: Parkinson caught five of six targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: The tight end's six targets tied Kyren Williams for second on the team behind Puka Nacua's seven on a day the Rams couldn't move the ball. Parkinson entered Sunday with four catches for 24 yards on seven targets. He can largely be ignored in fantasy football as the Rams' main blocking tight end.

injuries.shortComment: Corum produced 42 yards on nine carries and reeled in both of his targets for 18 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 18-16 loss against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Corum was only two touches behind the Rams' clear lead RB Kyren Williams, which marked the second-smallest gap between the two in a game this season. Moreover, Corum took advantage of Sunday's slightly expanded workload by reaching the end zone for the second time in as many contests. So far, his 56 touches have equated to 314 yards from scrimmage and two TDs, and he'll aim for another somewhat even split with Williams next Sunday at Las Vegas.

injuries.shortComment: Williams notched 10 carries for 50 yards and recorded three catches (on six targets) for 17 yards during Sunday's 18-16 defeat to the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Williams' rush total represents a season low as he ceded nine carries to reserve RB Blake Corum. Additionally, Williams also didn't reach the end zone for only the second time in six games in 2026, while Corum recorded a TD for the second consecutive contest. Williams is nearly exactly doubling up Corum in terms of touches on the campaign (110 versus 56), so he figures to be the better bet for a fantasy-relevant performance next Sunday in Las Vegas.

injuries.shortComment: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback against the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: As the inactive emergency third option, Simpson cannot play in Sunday's contest unless both Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injuries.shortComment: Atwell (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Atwell is a healthy scratch for Sunday's contest. Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Alex Bachman are the five active receivers over Atwell.

injuries.shortComment: The Rams activated Trost (hamstring) from injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Trost also has no injury designation and should make his NFL regular-season debut against Arizona on Sunday. With starting LT Alaric Jackson suspended for Week 6, Trost could serve as the swing tackle behind David Quessenberry and Warren McClendon.

injuries.shortComment: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Friday that Wright (foot) will play in Sunday's game against the Jets, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
injuries.longComment: It remains to be seen if Wright will have a designation on the final injury report, but either way, it sounds like he's ready to play. He'll likely be the team's No. 2 RB behind Ollie Gordon, who has dominated backfield work since De'Von Achane suffered an ACL tear.

injuries.shortComment: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Friday that Douglas (ankle) will play Sunday against the Jets, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
injuries.longComment: The rookie wideout hasn't played since Week 2 due to an ankle sprain. He'll return to a wideout corps that has been featuring Malik Washington and fellow rookies Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman as its three-wide set. Douglas should push Bell for an every-down role alongside Washington, bumping Coleman down the depth chart. Only Washington is a reliable fantasy option in 12-team leagues.

injuries.shortComment: Kacmarek (hamstring) was limited in Thursday's practice, but he said he expects to play Sunday versus the Jets, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
injuries.longComment: Kacmarek is dealing with a hamstring issue, though it's not clear when he suffered the injury given that Miami was on bye this past weekend. Regardless, the rookie tight end is anticipating being on the field Week 7 despite being limited in practice both Wednesday and Thursday. Kacmarek hasn't been a major factor in Miami's passing game thus far, recording just three catches on six targets for 24 yards through five contests.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Savaiinaea (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Savaiinaea injured his ankle during the Dolphins' Week 5 loss to the Bengals. The second-year offensive lineman had extra time to recover thanks to the Week 6 bye, and given his ability to practice in full Wednesday, Savaiinaea should start at right guard against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: The Dolphins opened the 21-day practice window for Louis (knee) on Wednesday, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Louis progressed enough in his recovery from a knee injury to be cleared to practice Wednesday, and he was a limited participant in his return. He'll likely need to log consecutive full practices before being activated from IR, but there's a chance that he is given the green light to play against the Jets on Sunday. The rookie fourth-rounder's return would bolster the Dolphins' depth in the secondary and give the team another contributor on special teams.

injuries.shortComment: Brents (neck) was a full participant at the Dolphins' practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Brents suffered a stinger in the team's Week 5 loss to the Bengals, but he now appears to be back to 100 percent following the team's bye week. The cornerback will be back in his starting role in Miami's secondary versus the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Joly (concussion) did not appear on the Dolphins' injury report Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Joly was inactive for the team's Week 5 loss to the Bengals while recovering from a concussion, but he now appears to be back to full health after Miami's bye week. The tight end will be back in his depth role behind starter Greg Dulcich on Sunday against the Jets.

injuries.shortComment: Taaffe (chest) did not appear on the Dolphins' injury report Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Taaffe suffered a chest injury in Week 5 versus the Bengals, but he appears to be back to full health after the team's bye week. The 23-year-old is all set to operate in his role as a primary reserve option at safety Sunday against the Jets.

injuries.shortComment: Willis was a full participant in Wednesday's practice after being listed on the Dolphins' injury report with a right thumb issue,  David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Willis wasn't spotted throwing in an informal practice during the Dolphins' Week 6 bye due to an unspecified reason, but the thumb issue provides an explanation. After a week off to rest and recover, Willis kicked off Week 7 prep with no limitations and will be ready to start in Sunday's game against the Jets.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Wayne was claimed off waivers by the Dolphins on Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: Wayne was waived by the Texans on Monday, though he was quickly scooped up by the Dolphins on Tuesday. The 26-year-old appeared in nine regular-season games for Houston across three seasons, totaling six grabs (14 targets) for 65 yards.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Dulcich caught four of five targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Bengals.
injuries.longComment: Dulcich finished second on the team in catches, and his five targets were third most for Miami. The tight end rebounded nicely after failing to garner a target over 20 offensive snaps in Week 4 against Minnesota's tough defense, and he now has caught 13 of 17 targets for 127 yards over five contests this season.

injuries.shortComment: Coleman caught three of seven targets for 30 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Bengals.
injuries.longComment: Coleman finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wide receiver Malik Washington (eight). Coleman's most significant moment in Week 5 came in the fourth quarter when he reeled in a three-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Malik Willis. Coleman has now caught five of 17 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown over five contests this season.

injuries.shortComment: Washington secured six of eight targets for 43 yards, rushed once for 18 yards, returned two kickoffs for 45 yards and ran back one punt for 28 yards in the Dolphins' 31-24 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Washington led the Dolphins across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets during Caleb Douglas' third straight absence because of an ankle injury, although the middle total was relatively modest on an afternoon in which Malik Willis threw for just 137 yards. Washington's catch total was also a new season high, and he's now upped his reception tally over that of the previous week in four consecutive contests. Washington will remain a relevant asset in deeper PPR formats and as a DFS dart throw in a Week 7 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Gordon rushed 18 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins' 31-24 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Gordon turned in a useful fantasy performance in the lead role once again, even as he navigated a brief exit from the game due to an undisclosed injury in the second half. The second-year back was able to still handle a robust workload despite the Dolphins trailing for the majority of the game, and he finished with a new career high in rush attempts. Gordon also recorded a rushing touchdown for the third straight game when he went in from one yard with just over eight minutes remaining in the first quarter, and he should continue to helm Miami's ground attack in a Week 7 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Brooks (foot) returned to Sunday's game against the Bengals in the third quarter, Travis Wingfield of the Dolphins' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: After exiting in the first half with the foot injury, Brooks was given the green light to check back into the contest upon receiving treatment.

injuries.shortComment: Woodard (ankle) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
injuries.longComment: Woodard left early in Week 4 but upgraded to limited participation in practice Friday.

injuries.shortComment: The Dolphins activated Grant (toe) from injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Grant opened Week 5 prep with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday. He does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Bengals, so Grant's activation from IR means he'll be available to make his 2026 regular-season debut. The 2025 first-rounder figures to operate in a rotational role at defensive tackle behind Jordan Phillips and Zach Sieler.

injuries.shortComment: Trader (shin) does not have an injury designation against the Bengals on Sunday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Trader opened Week 5 prep with consecutive limited practices, but he avoided an injury tag after logging a full session Friday. The second-year safety has 19 tackles (nine solo) and two pass defenses (one interception) through the first four games of the regular season.

injuries.shortComment: Darrisaw (concussion) was a full participant at the Vikings practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Darrisaw has opened the week with back-to-back full practices, but it is unclear if he has cleared concussion protocol quite yet. The offensive lineman's status for Week 7 will become much more clear when Minnesota releases its final injury report of the week following Friday's practice.

injuries.shortComment: Hockenson (concussion) was listed as a full participant Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Hockenson is inching closer to clearing the protocol for head injuries after sustaining a concussion during the Vikings' Week 5 win at New Orleans. At the very least, he must gain clearance from an independent neurologist in order to suit up again Sunday against the Colts.

injuries.shortComment: Mason (thumb) practiced fully Thursday.
injuries.longComment: With back-to-back uncapped sessions under his belt so far this week, Mason appears to be putting himself in a position to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Colts. He's seeking his first game action since Week 1, when he suffered a small fracture in his thumb that required surgery. If he's able to return this weekend, Mason likely will resume a timeshare with Aaron Jones out of the Vikings backfield.

injuries.shortComment: Jefferson (ankle) practiced in full Thursday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
injuries.longComment: Jefferson's upgrade from limited Wednesday to uncapped one day later indicates that the ankle injury that has bothered him since the middle of a Week 3 win at Tampa Bay is behind him. He'll be taking on a Colts defense Sunday that has allowed the 10th-most yards per target (8.6) to opposing wide receivers this season.

injuries.shortComment: Demmings (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Demmings missed each of the Vikings' two games prior to the Week 6 bye due to a hamstring injury. His full practice Wednesday indicates that he's fully healthy and will be available for Sunday's game against the Colts. The rookie fifth-rounder has served mostly on special teams, but his return gives the Vikings additional depth in the secondary.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Addison (hamstring) will participate in practice Wednesday, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Addison sat out the Vikings' last game Week 5 at New Orleans due to a sore hamstring, but with the benefit of a bye week, it appears he'll go down as at least a limited participant to kick off Week 7 prep. Wednesday's practice report will reveal his activity level.

injuries.shortComment: Jennings did not reel in his only target during Sunday's 23-13 win at New Orleans.
injuries.longComment: Jennings again got the second most snaps at wide receiver for the Vikings (47) in Week 5 with Jordan Addison (hamstring) out, but it only translated to one target on the afternoon. Jennings has failed to draw more than two targets in any game so far this season, and his role could be further diminished after Minnesota's bye in Week 6 if Addison is able to return to action.

injuries.shortComment: Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts and both extra-point tries during the Vikings' 23-13 win over the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Reichard got the Vikings on the board early in the first quarter on a 40-yard field goal before connecting on kicks from 54 and 55 yards in the second and fourth quarter, respectively. Reichard has made at least three field goals in each of his last four games and is 15-for-15 on field-goal tries through five games, which is second-best in the NFL behind Spencer Shrader (16-for-16). Reichard is also one of five kickers who have made at least five field goals from 50-plus yards. The Vikings will be on a bye for Week 6 before welcoming in the Colts for Week 7 on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Murray completed 24 of 30 passes for 229 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while adding 10 rushes for 51 yards in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the Saints on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
injuries.longComment: Murray completed a season-high 80.0 percent of his passes while patiently carving up the Saints defense Sunday, and the returning Justin Jefferson unsurprisingly accounted for a significant chunk of the quarterback's production through the air with a 6-79-1 line on seven targets. Murray's yardage total was his second-highest of the season as well, trailing only the 247 he generated against the Dolphins in Week 4. The 2019 first overall pick may be starting to hit his stride in head coach Kevin O'Connell's offense, and he'll look to further master the scheme during a Week 6 bye before returning to action in a Week 7 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Jones rushed 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for four yards in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Jones continued handling the workhorse role in Minnesota's backfield, and he finished Sunday's contest with a new season high in carries despite exiting the game for a spell due to a leg issue. Jones added his second rushing touchdown of the season on an eight-yard run early in the fourth quarter, while the 100-yard effort was his second of the campaign. Sunday marked Jones' backfield mate Jordan Mason's fourth absence while on injured reserve due to a thumb injury, and it remains to be seen if the latter will be ready to suit up and put a dent in Jones' opportunities during a Week 7 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Jurgens (elbow) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Jurgens was activated from IR on Saturday. The offensive lineman has recovered from his elbow injury and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Yurosek (ankle) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Saints, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Yurosek was activated from the Vikings' injured reserve Saturday, just in time for Week 5. The 24-year-old has yet to play in the 2026 season. He is expected to add depth behind T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew versus the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: Thorson (hamstring) was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Thorson missed Sunday's Week 4 win over Miami due to his hamstring injury. However, with a pair of full practices to begin Week 5 prep, he's probably good to go for Week 5 versus New Orleans. Thorson should thus reclaim his role as the Vikings' punter.

injuries.shortComment: Cashman recorded eight tackles (three solo) and a fumble recovery during Sunday's 15-10 win versus the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: In a game where Miami's offense simply couldn't stay on the field, Cashman only played 38 defensive snaps. Nevertheless, he managed to rack up seven-plus tackles for his 15th straight contest going back to last season. He's a solid IDP consideration in most formats going into a Week 5 tilt at New Orleans.

injuries.shortComment: Jackson (knee) was placed on injured reserve by the Vikings on Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: Jackson suffered a torn meniscus during Sunday's 15-10 win over Miami, and he was already set to miss the rest of the regular season, so Tuesday's move to the IR comes as no surprise. Joe Huber is the top candidate to take over as Minnesota's starting left guard in Jackson's absence.

injuries.shortComment: Claiborne carried the ball three times for 12 yards during Minnesota's win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Claiborne continued to serve a limited role behind Aaron Jones even with Jordan Mason (thumb) on injured reserve. Claiborne will look to be more involved offensively during next week's matchup versus the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: Metellus recorded nine tackles (four solo), including 0.5 sacks, and a defensed pass Sunday against Tampa Bay in a 23-16 victory.
injuries.longComment: Metellus logged the second-most tackles on Minnesota behind Eric Wilson (11). One of his stops was an assisted sack of Baker Mayfield on the first play of the fourth quarter. Metellus has played every defensive snap for the Vikings so far this season and has racked up 20 tackles and two pass defenses through three contests.

injuries.shortComment: Rodgers logged six tackles (two solo) and an interception in Sunday's 23-16 victory over Tampa Bay.
injuries.longComment: Minnesota led by seven points late in the fourth quarter when Rodgers picked off rookie Jalon Daniels on a last-second heave that drifted just short of the end zone. It was Rodgers' first interception of the season and the fifth of his six-year career. The veteran cornerback emerged as a key starter for Minnesota last season and has played nearly every defensive snap for the team so far in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson finished Sunday's 23-16 victory over Tampa Bay with 10 tackles, including 1.5 sacks, and one defensed pass.
injuries.longComment: Wilson not only led Minnesota with 10 stops, he was also responsible for 1.5 of the team's six total sacks. The veteran linebacker recorded a career-high 6.5 sacks across 17 regular-season games with the Vikings last year, as he's benefitted statistically from being in defensive coordinator Brian Flores' blitz-happy system. Wilson also surpassed 100 tackles for the second time in his career last year and is on pace to do so again in 2026 with 20 stops through three contests.

injuries.shortComment: The Vikings placed Oliver (biceps) on injured reserve Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Oliver's move to IR was expected after the tight end was diagnosed with a torn bicep Monday. The tight end will likely miss most, if not all, of the 2026 season as he recovers from surgery. T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew are now the only tight ends on the Vikings' roster, meaning practice-squad elevations ahead of Week 4 will likely include at least one more option at the position. The Vikings signed linebacker Kyle Van Noy to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

injuries.shortComment: Henderson rushed three times for nine yards and secured both targets for 14 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Henderson's modest numbers underscore how modest a role he filled in the high-scoring loss. Rhamondre Stevenson had just six carries in his own right, but he also recorded a team-high 93 receiving yards on five catches. Henderson's rush attempts and rushing yards were both season lows, and the second-year back will look to bounce back in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Henry secured all seven targets for 71 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: The veteran tight end was a key contributor throughout the night, finishing with team-high figures in receptions and targets while ending second in receiving yards. All three components of Henry's receiving line also were season-high figures, and he now has between 44 and 71 receiving yards in four consecutive games. Henry will take a 26-296-2 line on 31 targets into a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Borregales made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three extra-point tries Thursday in a Week 7 loss to the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Borregales was limited to extra-point tries until the Patriots' final drive of the game, when the kicker nailed a 47-yard field goal with less than a minute remaining to bring his team to within six points ahead of an unsuccessful onside kick. The second-year pro has been held to just four FG attempts -- all of which he has made -- over his past four contests after going 5-for-7 across New England's first three games of the season. The lower volume is largely due to the Patriots' improvement on offense over that four-game stretch, as Borregales has gone 14-for-15 on point-after attempts during that span.

injuries.shortComment: Brown brought in three of six targets for 48 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Brown entered the night looking to put a fairly forgettable Week 6 return from injury behind him, but the veteran wideout could only slightly improve his numbers in the high-scoring loss. He was fairly quiet until the second half, when he had 16- and 14-yard grabs. Brown did finish second in targets on the night for New England, but Drake Maye focused most on tight end Hunter Henry and running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who saw a combined 12 targets. With Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder) out for at least three more games, Brown will have a chance to see elevated volume in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Stevenson rushed six times for 22 yards and brought in all five targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Stevenson had another tough day on the ground, especially considering he gained 13 of his 22 yards on one carry. However, the veteran back had a standout performance as a receiver, leading the Patriots in receiving yards on the night with a big hand from a weaving 48-yard touchdown catch off an end-of-half screen play. Stevenson is now averaging just 3.7 yards per carry across the first seven games of the campaign, but he's up to a 20-204-1 receiving line on 24 targets heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Maye completed 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards with two touchdowns and one interception while adding four rushes for 26 yards and another score in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Maye's final line was one that could have easily been generated in victory, but the 2024 first-round pick couldn't quite help the Patriots keep pace with the high-powered Bears offense. Nevertheless, he was able to post his second 300-yard effort in the last three games, while also tossing multiple touchdowns for the fourth straight contest. Maye connected with Rhamondre Stevenson and Eli Raridon from 48 and 30 yards, respectively, for those two scoring strikes, the former coming off a screen pass on the last snap of the first half. Those big plays were preceded by Maye's seven-yard scoring run early in the second quarter, and he also pulled his season completion rate up to 65.9 percent with Thursday's highly efficient effort. The third-year signal-caller should have a good opportunity to stay hot in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Vera-Tucker (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve by the Patriots on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Vera-Tucker suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 6 win over the Jets, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering. In his absence, Walter Rouse will take over as the team's starting left tackle Thursday night versus the Bears.

injuries.shortComment: Moses (foot) is officially active for Thursday's game at Chicago.
injuries.longComment: Moses was forced out of the Patriots' contest in Week 6 versus the Jets due to a foot injury after just nine snaps, and he was seen wearing a walking boot after that game. Now, despite a short turnaround and having been limited at practice all week, he's in line to play Thursday. He should start at right tackle in Week 7.

injuries.shortComment: Woodson (shoulder) is officially active for Thursday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Woodson has been nursing a nagging shoulder issue since picking it up back in Week 2 versus the Steelers, but he'll tough it out for the fourth straight contest in Week 7. He projects to start at safety next to veteran Kevin Byard on Thursday.

injuries.shortComment: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive and designated as New England's emergency third quarterback for Thursday's matchup versus Chicago.
injuries.longComment: This has become the routine for Morton, who has worked as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback every week so far this season. The role has yet to land the rookie QB any game reps, and he'll be eligible to enter Thursday's contest only if both quarterbacks ahead of him (Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito) are forced to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

injuries.shortComment: Elliss (chest) is officially active for Thursday's game at Chicago.
injuries.longComment: Elliss was able to practice at full speed during the week despite the chest issue he was tending to, and it won't hold him out of action on gameday, either. He's on the fringe of the IDP radar in some formats for a Week 7 matchup against a run-first Bears offense.

injuries.shortComment: Byard (chest) is officially active for Thursday's game at Chicago.
injuries.longComment: Byard dealt with a minor chest issue during the week that stuck him with a 'questionable' tag Wednesday, but as expected, he'll be available for Week 7. He figures to play a near-every down role against a run-heavy Chicago offense.

injuries.shortComment: Gonzalez (illness) is listed as active for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Gonzalez was a late addition to the Patriots' injury report ahead of Thursday's kickoff, but he subsequently participated in warmups and is in line to be able to play through his illness after all. In four games thus far, the star cornerback, who anchors New England's secondary, has recorded 14 tackles and five passes defended.

injuries.shortComment: inactive
injuries.longComment: inactive

injuries.shortComment: Canada (hamstring) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Canada, Carlton Davis (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) will all be sidelined for Thursday night's contest, which leaves Christian Gonzalez and Charles Woods as the starters at outside cornerback while Kindle Vildor and Elliott Davison provide depth. It will be the fourth consecutive game that Canada will miss due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to return is Week 8 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Prunty (hamstring) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Chicago.
injuries.longComment: Prunty will be sidelined for a third-straight game due to a hamstring injury that he picked up during the Patriots' Week 4 win over the Bills. With Carlton Davis (neck) and Channing Canada (hamstring) also ruled out, Charles Woods and Christian Gonzalez will serve as the Patriots' starting outside cornerbacks for Thursday night's game while Elliott Davison and Kindle Vildor provide depth at the position. Prunty's next chance to play is Week 8 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Brown (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Brown injured his knee during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets. He was held out of all three practices during Week 7 prep, and with both Brown and Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) sidelined Thursday, the Patriots will likely turn to Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse to serve as the starting guards against Chicago. Brown will aim to recover enough to return for Week 8 against Miami on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Davis (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Davis did not participate in Monday's practice but ended the Patriots' short Week 7 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. Despite the upgrade in practice participation, the cornerback is not quite ready to return to the field and will miss his third consecutive game with a neck injury. Charles Woods should once again start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback.

injuries.shortComment: Bryant (ankle) was a full participant at the Patriots' practice Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: Bryant has opened the week with back-to-back full sessions with the Patriots, and he may be trending toward a return to action in the near future. The offensive lineman has missed the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point after picking up an ankle injury during the preseason, but the team opened his 21-day practice window Wednesday. With New England traveling to face the Bears on Thursday, Bryant may not be ready to go in advance of Week 7, but Wednesday's injury report will provide more clarity toward his status.

injuries.shortComment: Kiner rushed 11 times for 57 yards while also adding 88 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Kiner stepped into a more prominent role in the backfield behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson in Week 6. With Henderson limited by an ankle injury, Kiner was able to log four more carries than Henderson's seven. Additionally, Kiner averaged 5.2 yards per carry, which was double the 2.6 YPC that Stevenson produced over 14 totes. It's unclear what role Kiner will play when Henderson is back to full health, but he certainly proved he can be productive with an increased workload.

injuries.shortComment: Doubs (shoulder) is hopeful to return after the Patriots' Week 11 bye and isn't expected to face a long-term absence, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: With Doubs already on injured reserve, this report offers a more encouraging timeline after Sunday's shoulder injury. He'll still need to miss at least four games, but a possible return after the bye would keep the Patriots from being without one of their key wide receivers for an extended stretch. Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be in line for increased snaps alongside A.J. Brown and slot man DeMario Douglas with Doubs sidelined.

injuries.shortComment: Douglas caught seven of eight targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: A.J. Brown returned to the lineup from his ankle injury and led the team with 10 targets, but he dropped multiple passes and finished with a 3-27-0 receiving line. After Romeo Doubs left with a shoulder injury early in the first half following a long touchdown grab, Douglas stepped into an increased offensive role. He ran 26 routes on Drake Maye's 35 dropbacks, and Douglas caught a nine-yard touchdown in the second quarter. He's posted back-to-back big box scores after logging 4-65-2 receiving last Sunday against Las Vegas. The Patriots' slot man doesn't have a big fantasy ceiling but looks like a passable WR4 during bye-week crunches headed into Thursday night's game against the Bears.

injuries.shortComment: Campbell (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Campbell sprained his right MCL in the Patriots' Week 5 win over the Raiders. The offensive tackle logged three limited practices during Week 6 prep and will attempt to play through the injury in Sunday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Elliss (calf) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Elliss was limited earlier in the practice week and will return to the lineup after missing the previous three games. The 31-year-old linebacker has recorded 24 tackles (11 solo) and one pass breakup across three starts this season.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Kamara (back) was limited at Friday's practice but does not have an injury designation for Week 7, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Kamara did not get a full practice in all week, but it appears that was simply for management purposes, as he will not head into Week 7 with any sort of injury tag. He shared the backfield duties with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson each of the last three weeks, and with Travis Etienne (hamstring) spending at least one more game on injured reserve, he figures to do the same Sunday in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Donaldson (shoulder) practiced without limitations Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Donaldson upgraded to full participation Thursday while Alvin Kamara (back) was limited for a second consecutive practice. Heading into Sunday's overseas showdown against the Steelers, Donaldson has been working as the Saints' third option in the backfield behind Kamara and Kendre Miller while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is on IR. Donaldson has accumulated 82 scrimmage yards on 16 touches over the past three games.

injuries.shortComment: Riley (neck) was a full participant in practice Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Riley began the week as a full participant in Wednesday's practice after exiting early in Week 6 with a neck injury. His unrestricted availability suggests he will be back in his starting spot Sunday for Week 7.

injuries.shortComment: McKinstry (illness) was a full participant at the Saints' practice Wednesday, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.longComment: McKinstry left the team's 34-27 win over the Giants in Week 6 with a migraine, but he is now back to full health ahead of Week 7. The 24-year-old will be tasked with trying to slow down DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard in Sunday's matchup with the Steelers in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Tuesday that Tyson (hamstring) is "getting closer" but won't practice this week, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
injuries.longComment: Tyson made the trip to Paris ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Steelers, but he's not ready to have his 21-day practice window opened just yet. While the Saints haven't provided many specifics regarding where Tyson stands in his recovery from a right hamstring strain beyond noting that he's "improving," the team has a bye coming Week 8, so rookie wideout will be afforded more time to get closer to 100 percent before potentially getting back on the field. If Tyson is able to resume practicing coming out of the bye week, he could be a candidate to make his NFL debut as soon as Nov. 8, when the Saints host the Browns.

injuries.shortComment: Werner recorded 11 total tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pass defensed during Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Werner was able to register double-digit stops for the second straight week and third time overall this season. The linebacker was also able to get to the quarterback in Week 6, sacking Jameis Winston in the second quarter. Through six games so far this year, Werner has compiled 46 total tackles (23 solo), including 2.0 sacks, while also producing two passes defensed.

injuries.shortComment: Emerson recorded seven solo tackles and four passes defensed, including two interceptions, during Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Emerson was all over the field in Week 6, finishing second on the team in tackles behind linebacker Pete Werner (11). The cornerback was thrust into a more prominent role in the secondary after Kool-Aid McKinstry was forced out of the game with a migraine, and Emerson definitely didn't disappoint. He was able to reel in a pair of interceptions, picking off Jameis Winston in the third quarter before jumping in front of a pass from J.J. McCarthy one quarter later.

injuries.shortComment: Carlson made two of his three field-goal attempts and all four PATs in the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Carlson made field goals from 51 and 58 yards while missing a 55-yard kick in the second quarter. Despite the miss, the kicker accounted for 10 of the Saints' 34 points and displayed a strong leg throughout the contest.

injuries.shortComment: Ruiz (knee) made the trip to Paris ahead of the Saints' game against the Steelers in Week 7, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.longComment: Ruiz was knocked out of Sunday's game against the Giants early after suffering a knee injury, but it looks like there's still a chance he could be available in Week 7. His activity at practice will be worth keeping an eye on when New Orleans begins preparing for the Paris matchup later in the week.

injuries.shortComment: Vele caught three of six targets for 42 yards during the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Vele was on the field for 66 of the Saints' 70 offensive snaps (94.3 percent), which was well ahead of fellow wideouts Chris Olave (42) and rookie Bryce Lance (36). Vele has seen at least six targets in each of the first six games of the regular season, and his 28-294-2 line on 43 targets already surpasses his totals across 13 regular-season games in 2025 (25-293-2 on 40 targets). Given his snap count, it wouldn't be surprising if Vele maintains his role in the offense even if Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR) returns, which could come as soon as Week 7 against the Steelers on Oct. 25 in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Lance caught two of four passes for nine yards and a touchdown during the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Lance's four targets were tied with Alvin Kamara for third most on the Saints behind Chris Olave (seven) and Devaughn Vele (six), with quarterback Tyler Shough completing only 16 of 30 passes. Both of Lance's catches came in the second quarter, the second of which was a two-yard touchdown that tied the game up at 10-10 with five seconds left in the first half. Lance's 36 offensive snaps were third most among New Orleans wide receivers, but his time as the team's WR3 could come to an end as soon as Week 7 against the Steelers on Oct. 25, given that rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR) is traveling with the team to Paris, per NewOrleans.Football.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson failed to reel in either of his targets during Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Johnson went without a catch in a regular-season contest for the first time since Week 3 of the 2024 campaign. The tight end had reeled in at least three passes in each of the team's first five games of the year. Over the last two weeks, Johnson has caught four of seven targets for 16 yards, and his next chance to get back on track will come in Week 7 against the Steelers in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Miller carried the ball 20 times for 70 yards and caught both his targets for zero yards in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Alvin Kamara missed time in the first half due to an undisclosed injury, and while he was able to return and make an impact as a pass catcher, Miller led the Saints in rushing yards and touches with 22. The 70 yards also represented his best total since Week 18 of his rookie season in 2023. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) not eligible to return until after a Week 8 bye, Miller should split reps in the backfield with Kamara once again in Week 7 against the Steelers in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Shough completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants. He added 32 yards and a TD on five carries.
injuries.longComment: While he didn't produce much yardage, Shough kept the Saints' offense humming, connecting with Bryce Lance, Alvin Kamara and Chris Olave for scores through the air while adding a one-yard touchdown on the ground in the third quarter. Shough has been playing through a couple broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which could help explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks, but the second-year QB showed he can be plenty productive despite the injury. Shough will take a 12:5 TD:INT through six games into a Week 7 tilt against the Steelers in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Olave caught four of seven targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: While he didn't see his usual volume on an afternoon in which Tyler Shough threw for only 144 yards, Olave was on the other end of one of the QB's three scores, hauling in an 18-yard TD early in the fourth quarter that proved to be crucial after the Giants staged a late, but unsuccessful, rally. Olave got double-digit targets in each of the first four games of the season, but over the last two contests he's been targeted just 13 times, posting an 8-89-1 line. He'll look to regain some steam in Paris for a Week 7 matchup against the Steelers.

injuries.shortComment: Wood (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Wood missed the Saints' last four games while on injured reserve due to a calf strain. He's been cleared to return Sunday and will resume his duties as the team's long snapper.

injuries.shortComment: Wright (concussion) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
injuries.longComment: The rookie fourth-rounder was unavailable for the Saints' Week 5 loss to the Vikings while in the league's concussion protocol. Wright has been cleared from protocol by an independent neurologist, and his return gives the Saints more depth on the offensive line.

injuries.shortComment: Broughton (illness) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants, Jeff Nowak of The Big 870 New Orleans reports.
injuries.longComment: Broughton was a full practice participant Friday, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He has six tackles (one solo), one forced fumble and a fumble recovery across four regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Thomas (groin) was a limited participant at the Giants' practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Thomas has been dealing with a groin injury for a series of weeks, but he has been able to play through it. The offensive lineman was a non-participant at practice Wednesday, but his ability to return to the field Thursday suggests that he will be good to go for Week 7 versus the Texans.

injuries.shortComment: Hood (concussion) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Hood wasn't able to practice at full speed Wednesday due to the concussion that knocked him out of the Giants' game versus the Saints in Week 6 early, but it didn't hold him back Thursday. He'll still have to clear league concussion protocol to be eligible to suit up in Week 7 at Houston, so there's no guarantee yet that he'll be available come Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Holland (concussion) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Holland will still need to go through the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before Sunday's game at Houston if he is going to play in that contest, but he's at least moving in the right direction. His activity at practice Friday could give some indication as to how close he is to being cleared for game action by an independent neurologist.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson (neck) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Johnson was back at practice Wednesday after being sidelined because of a neck injury in Week 6 versus the Saints, but another day later, it's still hindering him ahead of a Week 7 tilt at Houston. He'll probably have to log a full practice Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Newsome (concussion) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Newsome was knocked out of Sunday's game versus the Saints early by a concussion, and now his availability for Week 7 is in jeopardy. He'll have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before getting the green light to return to full-contact football activities, and whether he's able to return to practice Thursday or Friday may shed some light on any potential progress.

injuries.shortComment: Edmunds (shoulder) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Edmunds hurt his shoulder on the final play of Sunday's game versus the Saints, and now his availability for Week 7 is in question. Any chance he has of suiting up at Houston will likely hinge on whether he's able to get back on the practice field Thursday or Friday.

injuries.shortComment: The Giants designated Adebo (knee) to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Adebo was placed on the Giants' injured reserve following the team's Week 1 win over the Cowboys due to a knee injury. He's been sidelined for the last five games, but he's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice and was a limited participant in Wednesday's session, per Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site. Adebo would need to be activated from IR by Saturday at 4:00 p.m. ET in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Texans.

injuries.shortComment: Mooney (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Mooney wasn't cleared to return to this past Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints after injuring his neck in the fourth quarter, but he evidently responded well to treatment and faced no restrictions as the Giants returned to the field to begin Week 7 prep. With Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely demanding most of the looks in the passing game this season, Mooney has struggled to carve out consistent weekly volume. Through six appearances, Mooney has been targeted 19 times and has recorded an 8-109-0 receiving line while also adding 29 yards on two carries.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: McCarthy will start at quarterback in Week 7 against Houston, coach John Harbaugh confirmed Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Things had been trending in this direction after McCarthy's impressive performance in relief of Jameis Winston in Week 6. Harbaugh made it official Wednesday afternoon as the team looks to see what it has in the recently acquired McCarthy. He completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards with a touchdown and a pick and had a pair of 40-yard completions in limited action against the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: Winston is in line to serve as the Giants' backup quarterback Sunday against the Texans with the team planning to move forward with J.J. McCarthy as its starter in Week 7, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: After Jaxson Dart (knee) went down with a likely season-ending injury in a Week 2 loss to the Rams, Winston stepped in as the starter for the subsequent four games. Though Winston led the Giants to a respectable 2-1-1 record while completing 60.3 percent of his passes for 6.5 yards per attempt and a 7:4 TD:INT during that stretch, he had a rough showing in this past Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints before being pulled early in the fourth quarter. McCarthy proceeded to take over under center and nearly guided the Giants all the way back from a 24-point deficit, so he'll be rewarded with the starting nod for at least Week 7. Given that the 23-year-old McCarthy is a recent first-round pick who could have a longer-term future in New York or represent an appealing trade chip down the road, it wouldn't be surprising if he was given a long leash as the team's starter.

injuries.shortComment: Reese logged six tackles (four solo) and a fumble recovery during the Giants' loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Reese had another solid outing despite the loss, as he managed to recover the first fumble of his career. The 21-year-old has gotten off to a strong start in his rookie season, racking up 49 tackles (34 solo), including 1.0 sacks, an interception and a fumble recovery across his first six games.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Zvada made both of his field-goal attempts and his sole PAT in the Giants' 34-27 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Zvada had a strong Week 6 bounceback after going 2-for-5 on field-goal attempts in Week 5. The kicker made 30-yard and 41-yard field goals in the loss, so he still may struggle with distance and consistency as the season continues.

injuries.shortComment: Fields caught two of eight targets for 19 yards during the Giants' 34-27 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Fields' eight targets were a career high for the rookie third-rounder and third most among Giants pass catchers behind Malik Nabers (15) and Isaiah Likely (11). However, Fields had only two receptions to show for it, and he's logged two catches in each of the first six games of his NFL career. The Giants will hit the road for Week 7 against the Texans, and Fields could be working with J.J. McCarthy rather than Jameis Winston for that contest.

injuries.shortComment: Singletary turned four carries into 14 yards and hauled in his lone target for 19 yards during Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Singletary was back in action Sunday after being a healthy scratch in each of the Giants' three games prior to Week 6. Three of his four carries went for two yards or fewer, although he did log a nine-yard rush and 19-yard catch on back-to-back plays early in the fourth quarter. Singletary's 31 offensive snaps were most among Giants running backs, but the team's backfield situation is a mess, given Cam Skattebo saw the field for only six offensive snaps and did not record a carry. The Giants will hit the road for Week 7 against the Texans on Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Likely caught six of 11 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints.
injuries.longComment: The tight end came through with another big performance and connected with J.J. McCarthy on a 24-yard TD in the fourth quarter after the young QB had replaced Jameis Winston under center. It's reassuring that Likely remained involved even after the switch at quarterback, and he's seen double-digit targets in three straight games, delivering a 24-259-3 line on 36 targets as the team's No. 2 pass catcher behind Malik Nabers. Likely will look to keep rolling in Week 7 against the Texans, regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

injuries.shortComment: Skattebo played only six snaps and got zero carries or targets in the Giants' 34-27 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: One week after losing a key fumble in a 27-27 tie to the Commanders, Skattebo was removed from his starting job as the Giants backfield devolved into a four-man committee. Tyrone Tracy was the team's most productive back, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown but managing just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches, while Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches and Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries. With no one really stepping up in his place, Skattebo could return to a more significant role in Week 7 against the Texans, but it will be hard to trust any New York running back in fantasy lineups until one emerges from the pack.

injuries.shortComment: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Mitchell (finger) will play Sunday against the Dolphins, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
injuries.longComment: After missing the Jets' last four games, Mitchell will return to the lineup for New York's divisional matchup with Miami. It's unclear at this point what Mitchell's return to the lineup will mean for rookie Omar Cooper, as the two have been healthy and available for a total of five snaps together this season. The Dolphins have been good against opposing wide receivers, mainly because other teams have been able to run on them voluminously in positive game scripts.

injuries.shortComment: Hall (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
injuries.longComment: Hall appears to have a chance to return after missing the Jets' previous three games with the quadriceps issue, but he did just return to practice Thursday, so his status appears to genuinely be up in the air. If Hall isn't cleared to play, Braelon Allen would make another start in the backfield and handle the lion's share of the opportunities in a beautiful matchup against Miami's bad run defense.

injuries.shortComment: Mitchell (concussion) did not participate at the Jets' practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Mitchell was added to the injury report with a concussion Thursday, and he was forced to miss practice as a result. The offensive lineman seems to be unlikely to be available for Sunday's matchup with the Dolphins, but he'll have one more chance to practice Friday.

injuries.shortComment: Nwangwu (knee) did not participate at practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Nwangwu has now been unable to practice for two straight days because of a knee issue, and his availability for Week 7 is in serious doubt. He'll probably need to get back onto the practice field Friday to have a realistic chance of suiting up Sunday versus the Dolphins.

injuries.shortComment: Parham (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Wednesday was Parham's first practice since sustaining a knee injury in Week 3 against the Lions, which prevented him from playing in each of the Jets' three following games. He'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If Parham is cleared to return, then he would likely reclaim his starting job at left guard from Jordan Meredith.
