injuries.shortComment: Sherwood recorded 11 tackles (six solo), a forced fumble and a fumble recovery during Sunday's 26-19 loss at New England.
injuries.longComment: Sherwood made a huge hustle play on a third down early in the fourth quarter, punching the ball out of the arms of DeMario Douglas after chasing him down 39 yards beyond the line of scrimmage. He also recovered a fumble in the third quarter, and both turnovers set up Jets field goals. He profiles as a solid IDP option in many formats heading into a Week 7 tilt versus the Dolphins.

injuries.shortComment: Belton recorded nine tackles (four solo) and a pass defensed during Sunday's 26-19 loss at New England.
injuries.longComment: In a game where the Patriots were able to keep the ball on the ground for much of the day, Belton collected six-plus tackles for his fifth straight contest. He's on pace for a career year in that category, and he projects as a solid IDP option in many formats going into a Week 7 matchup versus the Dolphins.

injuries.shortComment: Davis rushed seven times for 16 yards and caught his only target for 10 yards during Sunday's 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Davis was on the field for just eight offensive snaps, but the running back had a touch on each of those snaps. He entered Week 6 having toted the rock just two times over five contests, so his increase in workload was a positive turn of events. With Breece Hall (quadriceps) still uncertain for Week 7, Davis could operate as the primary backup behind Braelon Allen again versus the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Patrick caught one of three targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Patrick was unable to have much of an impact in Week 6, finishing tied for fourth on the team in targets with tight end Kenyon Sadiq. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) still banged up, Patrick could get another crack at operating in a prominent role in New York's offense in Week 7 versus Miami.

injuries.shortComment: Sanders made all four of his field-goal attempts and his sole PAT in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Sanders had a stellar game, contributing 13 of the Jets' 19 total points in the contest. The kicker made field goals from 42, 36, 40 and 36 yards in the contest, keeping the Jets in the game until the very end.

injuries.shortComment: Taylor caught four of six targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Taylor put together his best performance of the year, setting new season highs in catches, yards and targets. The tight end now has caught nine of 12 targets for 55 yards over four games this season. With rookie Kenyon Sadiq also heavily involved at tight end, Taylor's upside will continue to be hard to gauge moving forward.

injuries.shortComment: Cooper brought in six of seven targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Making his return from a four-game stint on injured reserve due to an ankle sprain suffered on the opening possession of the season, Cooper hit the ground running and finished as the team leader in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The Indiana product also recorded his first NFL touchdown on a 48-yard strike from Geno Smith early in the third quarter, and his instant production despite the layoff gives his fantasy outlook a significant boost heading into a Week 7 home matchup against the Dolphins.

injuries.shortComment: Smith completed 20 of 30 passes for 252 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding two rushes for minus-1 yard in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Smith took three sacks while trying to play catch-up all afternoon, and in that context, his final numbers were all the more impressive. The veteran signal-caller helped the Jets claw back from a 17-3 halftime deficit to get within four entering the fourth quarter, but his interception at the Patriots' 24-yard line early in the period snuffed out a potential scoring opportunity. Smith has certainly given New York some much-needed veteran stability at the quarterback position and displayed encouraging chemistry with returning rookie Omar Cooper (6-103-1) on Sunday, so there's reason for optimism heading into a favorable Week 7 home matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Allen rushed 17 times for 78 yards and brought in both targets for 26 yards in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Allen served as the Jets' clear lead back during Breece Hall's second straight absence due to a quadriceps injury, and the former put together a productive effort that featured a new season high in receiving yards. Allen has acquitted himself very well as the No. 1 option over the last two games, posting 194 rushing yards and a touchdown alongside three receptions and the 26 receiving yards he accrued Sunday. If Hall remains sidelined in Week 7, Allen will get a crack at a beatable Dolphins defense at home.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson brought in four of six targets for 44 yards in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Wilson had an early catch and then had a quiet middle portion of the game before rounding out his line some in the fourth quarter. Wilson still finished with modest production overall, as his reception and receiving yards totals were both his second lowest of the campaign. Geno Smith has undergone his fair share of struggles in his return to New York this season, but Wilson remains his top target with 48 looks from the veteran signal-caller over the first six games. Wilson will take a 35-418-3 line into a Week 7 home matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Sadiq caught one of three targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Sadiq was able to clear concussion protocol during the week, but the rookie tight end has been playing through minor injuries all season. Since catching seven passes for 105 yards in Week 3 against the Lions, Sadiq has just three catches for 15 yards on 10 targets over the last three contests. He's become waiver-wire fodder in redraft leagues.

injuries.shortComment: Williams should continue to serve as the No. 3 wide receiver behind Garrett Wilson and Tim Patrick for Sunday's game against the Patriots due to the absence of Adonai Mitchell (finger).
injuries.longComment: Williams caught one of his two targets for 16 yards and rushed once for three yards in the Jets' Week 5 win over the Browns. The wide receiver should continue to see some attention from Geno Smith, but if Omar Cooper (ankle) is activated from IR for Sunday's game, that could change.

injuries.shortComment: Bailey recorded seven tackles (five solo), including 3.0 sacks, during the Jets' 17-12 win over the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: The Browns' offensive line had trouble containing Bailey and the Jets' pass rush Sunday, with New York sacking Deshaun Watson eight times. Three of those sacks were credited to Bailey, two of which were on third down and forced the Browns to punt on the next play. The Week 5 effort was the performance that the Jets were hoping to see out of the second overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft. Bailey is up to 5.0 sacks through five regular-season games, which leads the Jets and is tied with D.J. Wonnum for fourth most in the NFL behind Will Anderson (7.5), Greg Rousseau (6.0) and Dallas Turner (5.5).

injuries.shortComment: Stowers (quadriceps) was a full participant at the Eagles' practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Stowers has been on injured reserve since Sept. 12 while recovering from a pair of hamstring and quadriceps injuries. The tight end had his 21-day practice window opened Oct. 14, and his ability to open the week with a full practice is a good sign for his chances to return to action Monday night against Dallas.

injuries.shortComment: Calcaterra (back) was a full participant at the Eagles' practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Calcaterra was able to open the week with a full practice as he remains on injured reserve while recovering from a back injury. The tight end has been sidelined since the beginning of the season, but he could be on track to return to action Monday night against the Cowboys.

injuries.shortComment: Goedert (knee) was held out of Thursday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Goedert previously sat out Weeks 3 and 4 due to a sprained MCL in his right knee, but he's been able to handle 69- and 81-percent snap shares the last two games while compiling a 12-99-0 line on 17 targets. Thursday's DNP may be for maintenance of the previous injury, but his status nonetheless will be monitored as the week continues to get a sense of the tight end's chances to play Monday versus the Cowboys.

injuries.shortComment: Wicks (ankle) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Wicks made a very brief exit late in this past Sunday's loss to the Panthers but was able to return. With an ankle injury being cited as the reason for Thursday's absence, the nature of the injury has been revealed. Both Wicks and No. 1 WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) were DNPs to kick off Week 7 prep, so the situation bears watching to see if either of them will be able to play Monday against the Cowboys.

injuries.shortComment: Smith (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Smith wasn't present in the media-access portion of Thursday's session, and his previous hamstring issue appears to be the culprit for his absence to begin Week 7 prep. He thus will have two more chances to prove his health before the Eagles potentially tag him with a designation for Monday's game versus the Cowboys.

injuries.shortComment: Barkley (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
injuries.longComment: This marks Barkley's first official on-field work since he initially suffered a hamstring injury in Week 4 against the Rams. He consequently sat out Weeks 5 and 6, but his return to drills this week at least gives him a chance to suit up Monday versus the Cowboys. Barkley told Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer on Thursday that he wants to play in Week 7 but still needs to test out his hamstring over the next few days. Ultimately, Saturday's practice report will reveal Barkley's odds to return to action.

injuries.shortComment: DeJean posted five solo tackles and a pass defense in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers in Week 6.
injuries.longComment: DeJean has logged at least five tackles in each of the first six games of the regular season and has played every defensive snap in four of those contests. He's up to 39 tackles (23 solo) and five pass defenses (including one interception) on the season, and he's third on the Eagles in combined takcles behind Jihaad Campbell (47) and Zack Baun (42).

injuries.shortComment: Baun registered six tackles (four solo) and a pass defense during the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers in Week 6.
injuries.longComment: Baun was one of three Eagles players to play all 79 defensive snaps, and his six combined tackles were tied for third-most on the team behind Arnold Ebiketie (nine) and Andrew Mukuba (eight). Through five regular-season games, Baun has accumulated 42 tackles (22 solo) and four pass defenses, and he is on track to crack 100-plus tackles for a third consecutive year.

injuries.shortComment: Cooper caught one of two targets for nine yards and added 38 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Cooper saw his offensive workload decrease with the return of DeVonta Smith in Week 6, and, as a result, this was the first time he's failed to reel in multiple passes since Week 3. With Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon all active, Cooper's ceiling will be limited from a fantasy perspective moving forward.

injuries.shortComment: NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports that teams seeking help at wide receiver will likely call the Eagles about the status of Brown before the Nov. 10 deadline.
injuries.longComment: Brown's lone regular-season game this season was in Week 2 against the Titans, when he rushed for 12 yards on two carries and did not record a target. He missed the next three games due to an ankle injury and was a healthy scratch for Week 6 against the Panthers, and the veteran wide receiver doesn't appear to be in the Eagles' offensive gameplan moving forward. The Eagles have a 2-4 record, and with franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts (calf) likely out for the rest of the season, the team could be looking to trade Brown and other players by the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

injuries.shortComment: Elliott made both of his extra-point attempts during the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: With Jalen Hurts (calf) out for the year, Sunday was the Eagles' first game with Tanner McKee under center. The offense labored to get up and down the field, and it was the fifth time in six games that Elliott attempted zero or one field goals. Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26 could be a better night offensively for the Eagles, given that Dallas' defense ranks 30th in the league in yards allowed per game.

injuries.shortComment: Hurts (calf) is expected to be held out of football activities for multiple months and miss the rest of the season after new imaging over the weekend revealed several blood clots in his lungs, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
injuries.longComment: Initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot after being cleated in the left calf in an Oct. 4 loss to the Rams, Hurts had been cleared by doctors to play in Week 5 in the Eagles' loss to the Jaguars in London before more recent testing last week showed that the blood clot had moved. According to a statement released Monday by his agent, Nicole Lynn, Hurts now has been diagnosed with a deep vein thrombosis in the left calf, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. Hurts has gone on blood thinners to treat the blood clots, and while his prognosis is good and he's not expected to face any long-term health effects, he won't be able to participate in football activities until he's off blood thinners. With that in mind, Hurts isn't expected to make a push for a late-season return from injured reserve and instead will turn his focus toward returning to full health in 2027. The Eagles will move forward with Tanner McKee, Cole Payton and Joe Milton as their options at quarterback.

injuries.shortComment: McKee completed 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while adding one carry for no gain in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
injuries.longComment: McKee's completion total was impressive, but he averaged a modest 4.8 yards per attempt on the afternoon despite having DeVonta Smith back from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. McKee's longest completion of the day went for 19 yards to Smith on a fourth-quarter scoring strike, which brought Philadelphia to within five at the time. McKee ultimately wasn't able to complete the comeback in the first installment of what figures to be an extended starting assignment in place of Jalen Hurts (IR, calf), and he'll look to be more aggressive during a Week 7 home divisional clash with the Cowboys next Monday night.

injuries.shortComment: Pierce rushed 12 times for 35 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 15 yards in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Pierce handled all the running back carries for the Eagles with all of Saquon Barkley (hamstring), Tank Bigsby (IR, abdomen) and Will Shipley (IR, foot) unavailable. As his rushing line suggests, Pierce found running room mostly at a premium, but he managed his first touchdown on the ground since the 2024 season on a two-yard run late in the first half. Pierce also was surprisingly involved as a receiver with Tanner McKee quarterbacking the offense, and the veteran back will remain in a similar role in a Week 7 home matchup against the Cowboys next Monday night if Barkley remains out.

injuries.shortComment: Lemon caught three of six targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: The rookie wideout briefly exited Week 6 with an undisclosed injury but quickly returned and ended up running a team-high 45 routes on Tanner McKee's 49 dropbcks. It still didn't result in much production, as Lemon's six targets were a distant third on the team. The first-round wide receiver has just 18 catches for 127 yards and no touchdowns on 28 targets through six games. He can't be trusted as a fantasy starter headed into next Monday night's game against the Cowboys.

injuries.shortComment: Smith (concussion) won't return to Sunday's game against Carolina.
injuries.longComment: Smith took a hit from Chuba Hubbard in the second quarter. He exited for an evaluation in the medical tent and was then escorted to the locker room by the training staff. With Smith ruled out for the remainder of Week 6, the Eagles will need to rely on Jonathan Greenard, Arnold Ebiketie and Keyshawn James-Newby to fill the void.

injuries.shortComment: Watt (calf) practiced fully Friday and doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Saints.
injuries.longComment: Watt was limited by a calf injury Thursday, but he's good to go for Pittsburgh's Paris game against New Orleans. Through six games this season, the 32-year-old Watt has 15 tackles (10 solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery and a pick-six interception.

injuries.shortComment: Dowdle (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
injuries.longComment: The Steelers did not practice Friday because of poor weather in Paris, but if they had Dowdle would have been limited with the knee injury -- different than the toe issue he was dealing with previously -- for a third straight day. The Steelers will practice Saturday and could provide an update on Dowdle's status after the session concludes, otherwise his status for Week 7 will be revealed when Pittsburgh releases its inactives 90 minutes before Sunday's 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff.

injuries.shortComment: Echols (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's matchup with the Saints, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Echols suffered a hamstring injury in the first half of the team's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers, and he will now be forced to miss at least one additional contest as a result. The cornerback plays primarily on special teams, so his absence won't have much of an impact on the Steelers' defensive approach in Week 7.

injuries.shortComment: Joseph-Day (triceps) was placed on injured reserve by the Steelers on Thursday, Teresa Varley of the team's official website reports.
injuries.longComment: Joseph-Day is dealing with an apparent triceps injury, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering. In his absence, Gabriel Rubio and Kevin Jobity are both candidates to see an increase in workload on Pittsburgh's defensive line.

injuries.shortComment: The Steelers have ruled Skowronek (calf) out for Sunday's matchup against the Saints, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Skowronek did not participate in Wednesday's practice. He will now miss his second straight week due to a calf injury suffered in the Steelers' Week 5 win against the Colts. Kaden Wetjen may see some extra reps in his place.

injuries.shortComment: Elliott (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: It's the first time Elliott has logged a full practice since his 21-day window to return from injured reserve opened Oct. 8. The Steelers released Rayshawn Jenkins earlier Wednesday, and that's a potential sign that Elliott will be available to make his 2026 debut this Sunday against the Saints in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Brisker posted seven tackles (four solo) during the Steelers' 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Brisker played every single defensive snap for the fifth time in six games this season, and he has logged at least six tackles in each of those outings. He's up to 41 combined tackles in 2026 and is on track to crack 100 tackles for the third time in his NFL career and the first time since 2023, when he played for the Bears.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson recorded 11 tackles (seven solo) during Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.longComment: Payton led the Steelers in tackles Sunday, and it was the third time he's logged double-digit stops this season. The third-year linebacker is up to 55 combined tackles, which leads the Steelers and is eighth-most in the NFL. He should remain busy in Week 7 against the Saints, whose offense, led by QB Tyler Shough, put up 34 points in a win over the Giants in Week 6.

injuries.shortComment: Herbig recorded six solo tackles, including 2.0 sacks, during the Steelers' 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Herbig did not record a sack through the first five games of the regular season, but the fourth-year pro got to quarterback Jalon Daniels twice during Sunday's OT victory. Herbig is up to 18 tackles (13 solo) and one forced fumble through six regular-season games while working in a rotational role on defense.

injuries.shortComment: Boswell went 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts while making both of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 26-19 overtime win against Tampa Bay.
injuries.longComment: Boswell converted multiple field goals for the second week in a row and the fourth time overall in 2026. The kicker pulled his first field-goal attempt of the day wide left from 48 yards out in the first quarter, but he responded by adding makes from 52, 39 and 20 yards before the end of regulation. Boswell now has gone 13-for-17 on field-goal tries, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, while making all 12 of his PATs over the team's first six contests this year.

injuries.shortComment: Freiermuth caught two of three targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Bucs.
injuries.longComment: Freiermuth entered Week 6 questionable due to a calf injury, but he ended up running 41 routes on Aaron Rodgers' 56 dropbacks. The tight end just didn't do much in the box score and was targeted on just 6.1 percent of Rodgers' 49 pass attempts. Freiermuth has already scored four touchdowns this season but has just 180 receiving yards on 21 grabs across 29 targets through six games. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option.

injuries.shortComment: Metcalf caught 11 of 15 targets for 93 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.longComment: The targets and catches were season highs for Metcalf, while the veteran WR came up just short of his second 100-yard performance in the last three weeks. Metcalf will take a 30-318-1 line on 52 targets into a Week 7 clash with the Saints in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Warren carried the ball 14 times for 50 yards and caught two of four targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.longComment: While Warren still led the Steelers' backfield, his touch volume and production took a dip as Rico Dowdle returned from a three-game absence due to a toe injury, with Dowdle turning 10 touches into 49 scrimmage yards. As long as coach Mike McCarthy insists on using a timeshare between the two, Warren will be hard-pressed to repeat the outstanding numbers he compiled while Dowdle was on the shelf. Warren will try to make a bigger impact in Week 7 against the Saints in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Rodgers completed 33 of 49 passes for 253 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.longComment: Down 16-3 to begin the fourth quarter, Rodgers began the comeback with a five-yard TD pass to Darnell Washington before leading the Steelers on three straight field-goal drives. The veteran QB then put together a 12-play, 70-yard drive to begin OT that was capped with a six-yard score to Germie Bernard. Rodgers has tossed multiple touchdowns in four straight games, posting an 11:4 TD:INT over that stretch and giving him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 7 trip to Paris to face the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: Washington caught four of six targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Bucs.
injuries.longComment: The Steelers entered the fourth quarter trailing 16-3, but Washington sparked the comeback with a five-yard touchdown to make it 16-10. It was the big tight end's second touchdown of the season, and he's now recorded 15 grabs for 156 yards and the two scores on 22 targets through six games. He's on pace for a career year in the receiving department and is a preferred target of Aaron Rodgers near the goal line due to his sheer size advantage.

injuries.shortComment: Bernard caught 11 of 12 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Bucs.
injuries.longComment: With Michael Pittman (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) out for the Steelers, Bernard was the clear WR2 behind DK Metcalf and actually ran a team-high 54 routes on Aaron Rodgers' 56 dropbacks. Metcalf edged Bernard out in targets 15 to 12, while both players caught 11 passes. Pittman and Wilson are both required to miss at least two and three more games, respectively, so Bernard is locked into an every-down role for the immediate future. Rodgers has sung the rookie wideout's praises early this season, and it's reasonable to expect Bernard to remain a key part of the passing offense moving forward. He should be rostered in all fantasy formats.

injuries.shortComment: Dean (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
injuries.longComment: Dean was a limited participant throughout Week 6 prep. The cornerback is all set to suit up in Sunday's contest, likely playing through the remains of his ankle injury.

injuries.shortComment: Bosa (calf) did not participate at the 49ers' practice Thursday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Bosa was unable to practice for the second straight day to open the week as he continues to work his way back from a calf injury that has sidelined him since Week 2. The defensive lineman is all but guaranteed to miss a fifth straight game Sunday versus the Falcons, but the team expressed optimism that Bosa could return to action Nov. 8 against the Raiders, per Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com.

injuries.shortComment: Kirk (calf) was a full practice participant Thursday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Back-to-back full practices have Kirk trending in the right direction ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons. The 49ers have until Saturday to activate Kirk from IR ahead of Week 7 action, but if he's available this weekend he'd provide a boost to a WR corps dealing with injuries to both Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring).

injuries.shortComment: Evans (ribs/Achilles) didn't practice Thursday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Evans officially logged a second consecutive DNP after he made an early exit from Monday's win against the Commanders due to an aggravation of a right Achilles' injury, which head coach Kyle Shanahan has called soreness, per Wagoner. While Evans now has just one more chance to mix into drills this week, he's proved in the past that he doesn't require practice reps to be available on game days. Whether or not he has a chance to play Sunday in Atlanta will become known once the 49ers post their final Week 7 injury report Friday.

injuries.shortComment: Dugger (knee) was estimated to be a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: Dugger appears to have picked up a knee injury in the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Commanders. The strongside linebacker's ability to practice in the first Week 7 prep session is a strong sign that he should be able to suit up for Sunday's contest against the Falcons. Dugger will likely need to upgrade to full participation by Friday's session to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Williams (knee) was estimated to be a nonparticipant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: Williams likely sustained his knee injury in the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Commanders on Monday night. It is unclear how significant the defensive end's issue is. Still, he will need to achieve some level of practice participation by Friday to have any hope of suiting up for Sunday's game against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Sigle (ankle) was estimated to be a nonparticipant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: Sigle has not practiced since being diagnosed as week-to-week with the high ankle sprain he sustained in the 49ers' Week 4 win over the Broncos. Wednesday's injury report signals that Malik Mustapha is once again taking first-team reps at strong safety in Sigle's place in anticipation of the team's Week 7 game against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Samuel (hamstring) is not expected to practice Wednesday, Cam Inman of Bay Area News Group reports.
injuries.longComment: The 49ers are coming off a Monday Night Football win and therefore are not holding an official practice Wednesday. That being said, coach Kyle Shanahan said that Samuel would not be practicing. Samuel is working his way back from a hamstring injury, and the sense is that a return after the 49ers' Week 8 bye is more realistic at this stage.

injuries.shortComment: Warner totaled eight tackles (six solo) during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Warner was on the field for every single defensive snap for a fourth consecutive game, and he finished second on the 49ers in tackles behind Jaden Dugger (11). Warner has logged at least seven tackles in five of six regular-season games, and his 58 combined tackles are third-most in the NFL behind Alex Singleton (68) and Ernest Jones (59). The 49ers will hit the road for Week 7 against the Falcons on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Pineiro made his lone field-goal attempt and went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Pineiro's extra-point try late in the first quarter missed wide to the right, but he connected on a 33-yard field goal late in the third quarter to give the 49ers a 23-3 lead. Through six regular-season games, the veteran kicker has gone 6-for-9 on field-goal attempts and 19-for-22 on extra-point tries. He hasn't been the most accurate kicker, but Pineiro's scoring floor will remain elevated with a 49ers team that ranks third in the NFL in points per game (29.5) and ninth in yards per game (366.7).

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that Stout's removal from Monday's 23-17 win over the Commanders was due to an AC sprain in his shoulder, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Stout's practice reps during Week 6 prep were limited due to his shoulder injury. He was cleared to play Monday but was hampered by his injury, which led to Stout being replaced by Ashtyn Davis in the second half and finishing with two tackles over a season-low 25 snaps. Stout's practice participation over the coming days will provide some clarity on his status for Sunday's road game against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Greenlaw was reinstated by the NFL on Tuesday after he served a one-game suspension in Week 6, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Greenlaw was back at practice Tuesday after missing the team's 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday Night Football. The 29-year-old will return to his starting role at weakside linebacker in Week 7 against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Watkins caught his lone target for 22 yards during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Watkins connected with Brock Purdy for a big gain early in the second quarter, and all three of wideout's catches this season have gone for 20-plus yards. Watkins' 47 offensive snaps ended up leading all 49ers wide receivers, and the second-year pro's role in the passing game could expand in Week 7 against the Falcons, depending on the availability of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring).

injuries.shortComment: Cowing accrued zero targets during Monday's 23-17 win against Washington.
injuries.longComment: Despite the absence of Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and the premature exit of Mike Evans (Achilles), Cowing went without a catch for the fifth time this season. With neither Samuel nor Evans a lock to suit up in Week 7 versus the Falcons, Cowing might see more snaps alongside Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins. However, that may not be the case if Demarcus Robinson (ankle) can manage to get on the field after spending time on injured reserve since the Week 2 win over Miami.

injuries.shortComment: out
injuries.longComment: out

injuries.shortComment: Cooks brought in one of two targets for 13 yards in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Cooks unsurprisingly played a minor role in the air attack as one of four players with one catch on the night. The veteran wideout has two receptions for 20 yards and a touchdown on five targets over the three games for which he's been active to date, and with Demarcus Robinson (ankle) not likely to return from injured reserve until Week 8, Cooks is likely to suit up again in a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Black rushed eight times for 34 yards and brought in his only target for three yards in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Black logged half as many carries as Christian McCaffrey and a whopping nine fewer targets, cementing the pecking order in the 49ers' ground attack. However, Black is getting some nice complementary run as a rookie, as he's logged 45 carries over his first six games. Black has just three targets in that same span, however, so his fantasy upside will remain capped to a large degree in a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Kittle brought in five of eight targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Kittle was one of Brock Purdy's most effective targets on the night, finishing with the 49ers' second-highest reception, receiving yardage and target totals. The athletic tight end also was on the other end of Brock Purdy's one touchdown pass, recording an 11-yard scoring grab to cap off the opening possession of the night. Kittle has at least four receptions in five consecutive games and Monday night's receiving yardage total or higher in four of his first six contests of the season, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Purdy completed 21 of 29 passes for 264 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions while adding five rushes for 28 yards in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Purdy took multiple sacks for the second straight game after not being taken down over the first four contests, but the veteran signal-caller otherwise had a mostly clean night that included a robust average of 9.1 yards per attempt. Purdy's passing yardage total also was his third highest of the campaign, and he kept his season-long touchdown-pass streak alive when he connected with George Kittle on an 11-yard scoring strike to cap off the opening drive of the night. Purdy completed passes to seven different targets overall, and he now boasts a 14:2 TD:INT heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: McCaffrey rushed 16 times for 64 yards and two touchdowns and brought in nine of 10 targets for 53 yards in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.longComment: McCaffrey, who's been subject to a markedly lighter workload than usual over the first weeks of the campaign, recorded season highs in rush attempts, receptions, receiving yards and targets on a very busy night. The star running back also contributed his second multi-touchdown tally of the season, powering into the end zone on a pair of one-yard runs in the first half. McCaffrey logged twice as many carries and nine more targets than rookie backfield mate Kaelon Black, so there's no question who the leader of the ground attack is heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Gifford (groin) is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Commanders, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Gifford likely picked up the injury at some point during the first half of Monday's game. He was working in an elevated role defensively due to the absences of Dre Greenlaw (suspension) and Garret Wallow (hamstring), so Tatum Bethune should see a larger workload on defense for as long as Gifford is out of the game.

injuries.shortComment: Lock (elbow) was a limited practice participant Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Lock has now been limited in each of Seattle's past five practice sessions, though he was able to suit up last Thursday against Denver. It seems likely that he'll be active again for this Sunday's matchup against Kansas City, though Seattle's practice report Friday should provide more clarity in that regard. If Lock does indeed suit up Sunday, he'll again work as Sam Darnold's backup.

injuries.shortComment: Shaheed (hip) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Shaheed was limited Wednesday but appears to be on track for his normal role Sunday against the Chiefs. Playing behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp in an offense that likes to use multiple tight ends, Shaheed has yet to get going in the receiving department this season, as he has just 14 catches for 162 yards through six contests.

injuries.shortComment: Charbonnet (knee) practiced fully Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: In the midst of Seattle activating Charbonnet from the reserve/PUP list Thursday, Charbonnet now has strung together back-to-back uncapped sessions as he aims for his first game action since suffering a torn ACL in his left knee Jan. 17. In addition to head coach Mike Macdonald forecasting Charbonnet's "full week's worth of reps" Monday, he told Boyle that "you could see him on Sunday in some capacity." Even if Charbonnet is able to suit up this weekend against the Chiefs, he may enter a timeshare with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani off the bat instead of taking on a leading role.

injuries.shortComment: Arroyo (shoulder) was placed on injured reserve Thursday, and Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Arroyo will miss the remainder of the season.
injuries.longComment: Arroyo sustained a season-ending shoulder injury that will require surgery in last Thursday's loss to the Broncos. The 2025 second-round pick finishes his second NFL regular season with one catch for 17 yards on two targets in six games.

injuries.shortComment: Thomas (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Corbin K. Smith of EmeraldCitySpectrum.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Thomas has not participated in an on-field practice since sustaining his ankle injury in the Seahawks' Week 5 loss to the 49ers. The linebacker remains sidelined due to the injury, leaving Tyrice Knight (oblique) likely to fill in once again next to Ernest Jones in Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

injuries.shortComment: Bradford (knee) was designated to return from injured reserve by the Seahawks on Monday, John Boyle of the team's official website reports.
injuries.longComment: Bradford has been on IR since Sept. 23 while recovering from a knee injury, and he will now have his 21-day practice window opened ahead of Week 7. The offensive lineman is eligible to return to action against the Chiefs on Sunday, and his status at the team's first practice of the week Tuesday will shed more light on his chances to do so.

injuries.shortComment: Jones turned four carries into 20 yards and caught his only target for minus-1 yard during Thursday's 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos.
injuries.longComment: Jones played a total of 26 snaps (nine on offense, 17 on special teams) during Thursday's loss and operated as the clear RB3 behind Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. Jones was effective in the run game on limited carries, but he could lose his spot on the 53-man roster if Zach Charbonnet (knee) is activated from the reserve/PUP list ahead of the Seahawks' Week 7 home tilt against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Horton caught one of five targets for 13 yards and returned a punt for 13 yards during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday. He also logged one tackle.
injuries.longComment: Horton finished Thursday's game fourth on the Seahawks in targets but managed to catch only one pass from Sam Darnold, the latter of whom attempted a season-high 51 throws. Horton has a 5-67-1 receiving line on nine targets through five regular-season games, and he's firmly entrenched as the Seahawks' WR4 behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed. The Seahawks will head back home for Week 7 to host the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Emmanwori recorded seven tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday night's 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos.
injuries.longComment: After missing Week 1 recovering from offseason ankle surgery, Emmanwori has seen his playing time increase the last two weeks after being eased in to begin his 2026 season. He played a season-high 96.7 percent of the defensive snaps against Denver and has now logged 23 tackles (18 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one pass breakup across five contests.

injuries.shortComment: Jones recorded nine tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday night's 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos.
injuries.longComment: Jones has now recorded a sack in three straight games and has at least eight tackles in all six contests to kick off the 2026 campaign. He's up to 59 tackles (31 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and three pass breakups, with one interception, on 99.5 percent of the Seahawks' defensive snaps.

injuries.shortComment: Myers went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Myers opened Thursday's scoring with a 55-yard field goal late in the first quarter, with the veteran kicker taking advantage of the altitude at Mile High Stadium. He missed a 47-yarder in the third quarter but made up for it with a 34-yard field goal within the final seconds of the fourth, which forced Thursday's game into overtime. It was the first missed field goal of the season for Myers, who is 12-for-13 on field-goal attempts (including 3-for-3 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 14-for-15 on PATs through six regular-season games. The Seahawks will head back home for a Week 7 tilt against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Kupp caught five of 10 targets for 50 yards during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Kupp accumulated 15 targets through the first five games of the regular season, but the veteran wide receiver was peppered Thursday by Sam Darnold, who attempted a season-high 51 passes. It was the first time since Week 12 of the 2024 season (with the Rams) that Kupp saw double-digit targets, and he finished second in that category Thursday behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (16). Kupp's best days are behind him, but he's a valuable safety blanket for Darnold in the passing game. Kupp will bring a 16-179-1 receiving line (25 targets) into Seattle's Week 7 bout against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Barner caught three of four passes for 16 yards during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Barner wasn't targeted by Sam Darnold until late in the third quarter, and he finished a distant fourth behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed and Cooper Kupp in both catches and receiving yards. Barner has played 90 percent or more of the Seahawks' offensive snaps in five of six games this season, but he's also caught more than three passes just once (Week 3 against the Commanders). He also doesn't have a touchdown to his name this season after finding the end zone six times during the 2025 regular season. The Seahawks will look to break their two-game losing streak in Week 7 on Sunday, Oct. 25 against the Chiefs, whose defense has given up the third-most fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Price "should be looking at a sooner rather than later return after" the Seahawks' next game in Week 7, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Price was placed on injured reserve after Week 3 due to a lingering chest injury, and while he must miss one more contest to meet the minimum four-game requirement on the list, he appears as if he'll be ready to go when first eligible in Week 8 against the Bears on Monday, Nov. 2. In the meantime, the Seahawks are expected to get back fellow RB Zach Charbonnet (knee), so Price may be relegated to a lessened role once he's healthy enough to play again.

injuries.shortComment: Irving (illness) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Carolina, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.longComment: Irving returned to practice Thursday as a limited participant before upgrading to full participation Friday. With WR Emeka Egbuka (concussion) ruled out and QB Baker Mayfield (thumb) returning from a three-game absence, Irving should see the ball early and often this Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Mayfield (thumb) was a full participant in Friday's practice but is listed questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.longComment: Coach Todd Bowles already said earlier Friday that Mayfield is good to go for Week 7, so it would be a shock if the veteran quarterback isn't under center Sunday. It will be Mayfield's first action since Week 3 against the Vikings. Jalon Daniels will head back to QB2 duties once Mayfield is officially cleared.

injuries.shortComment: Egbuka (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.longComment: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said Egbuka was doubtful to play, but the official designation is more definitive. Chris Godwin, Ted Hurst and Tez Johnson figure to take most of the WR snaps this Sunday at Carolina.

injuries.shortComment: Rozeboom (finger) was placed on injured reserve by the Buccaneers on Thursday, Scott Smith of the team's official website reports.
injuries.longComment: Rozeboom will be forced to miss at least four games while recovering from a finger injury that he likely suffered in Week 6 against the Steelers. In his absence, SirVocea Dennis will stand to see an increase in workload at inside linebacker behind starters Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter.

injuries.shortComment: Sills (hamstring) was activated from injured reserve by the Buccaneers on Thursday, Scott Smith of the team's official website reports.
injuries.longComment: Sills had his 21-day practice window opened by the team Oct. 12, and he was able to open this week with back-to-back full practices. The wide receiver has been on IR since late August while recovering from a hamstring injury, but he will now slot in as a depth option behind Emeka Egbuka (concussion) and Chris Godwin moving forward this season.

injuries.shortComment: Tucker (quadriceps) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Tucker was sidelined by a quad injury in Week 6 versus the Steelers, but it now appears he's on track to suit up again in Week 7. Regular starter Bucky Irving did not participate at practice Wednesday due to an illness, and if he was unavailable for any reason for Sunday's matchup at Carolina, Tucker would probably be looking at an expanded role in the Bucs' backfield.

injuries.shortComment: Morrison (quadriceps) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: A quadriceps injury has sidelined Morrison for each of the Buccaneers' last three games, but his full session Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's NFC South showdown against the Panthers. Morrison should reclaim his starting job at outside cornerback opposite Zyon McCollum (illness) while rookie fourth-rounder Keionte Scott reverts to a rotational role in the secondary.

injuries.shortComment: Smith compiled 10 total tackles (three solo) during Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Smith was able to record double-digit stops for the first time this season, finishing third on the team behind linebacker Josiah Trotter (12) and cornerback Zyon McCollum (11). Smith has now registered 34 total tackles (20 solo), a pass defensed and a forced fumble over the first six contests of the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Scott recorded eight total tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to Pittsburgh.
injuries.longComment: Scott was able to register a season-high eight tackles, most notably bringing down Aaron Rodgers for his first career sack in the second quarter. The cornerback has now compiled 32 total tackles (27 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding two passes defensed over the first six regular-season games of his NFL career.

injuries.shortComment: Trotter recorded 12 total tackles (five solo) and a pass defensed during Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Trotter was sharp again in Week 6, registering double-digit stops for the third time this season while playing every defensive snap in the loss. The linebacker has now registered 52 total tackles (27 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pick-six over five games to open the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Walker recorded seven total tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, during Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to Pittsburgh.
injuries.longComment: Walker was able to register a season-high seven stops, most notably getting to Aaron Rodgers for a pair of sacks in the third and fourth quarters. The linebacker has now compiled 17 total tackles (10 solo), including 4.0 sacks, over six games to open the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: McLaughlin connected on all four of his field-goal attempts and converted his lone extra-point try during the Buccaneers' 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: It was the second time this season that McLaughlin made four field goals, including a 53-yarder in the dying seconds of the fourth quarter to force Sunday's game into overtime. He has yet to miss a kick this season, and his 14 made field goals are tied for third most in the NFL behind Spencer Shrader (18) and Will Reichard (15). The Buccaneers will be on the road for three of their next four games, starting with Week 7 against the Panthers on Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Hurst caught three of six targets for 40 yards during Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Hurst matched his season high in catches and receiving yards against Pittsburgh, reeling in multiple passes for the fourth time this year. The wide receiver has now caught 11 of 22 targets for 168 yards over six contests to begin his first NFL campaign, and he could receive a boost if Baker Mayfield (thumb) returns to action in Week 7 versus Carolina.

injuries.shortComment: Otton caught one of two targets for four yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Otton was targeted on just two of Jalon Daniels' 43 pass attempts, good for a lousy 4.7 percent share. The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and has been held below 40 yards in five of six contests. He's a low-floor fantasy option at the position who is best left on waivers.

injuries.shortComment: Godwin caught four of eight targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: For the fifth time in six games to begin the season, Godwin caught either three or four passes, and all six of his yardage totals have been between 25 and 46 yards. The veteran wideout also has yet to score a TD in 2026, and his lackluster production has come whether Baker Mayfield (thumb) or rookie Jalon Daniels has been under center. Godwin will try to find a way to break out in Week 7 against the Panthers.

injuries.shortComment: Daniels completed 22 of 43 passes for 164 yards and one touchdown with two interceptions in Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers. He added 39 rushing yards on four carries.
injuries.longComment: The rookie quarterback struggled in his third career start, but Daniels did connect with Emeka Egbuka on a two-yard score in the second quarter and had Tampa Bay in front 16-3 to begin the fourth. Once Aaron Rodgers began putting points on the board, though, Daniels buckled under the pressure and threw both his INTs. Baker Mayfield (thumb) has yet to return to practice, giving Daniels good odds of making his fourth straight start in Week 7 against the Panthers, but his 3:5 TD:INT since the veteran QB went down doesn't make him a very appealing fantasy option.

injuries.shortComment: Gainwell rushed two times for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers. He caught his only target for seven yards.
injuries.longComment: Even with Sean Tucker (quadriceps) inactive, Gainwell didn't see any sort of increase in his offensive role, getting out-carried 19 to two by Bucky Irving, who also saw three targets. Gainwell has 122 total yards through six games and can be sent to waivers in 10- and 12-team redraft fantasy leagues.

injuries.shortComment: Dennis (ankle/foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Ankle and foot injuries prevented Dennis from playing against the Cowboys in Week 5. He drew the questionable tag for Week 6 after logging a full practice Friday, and the fourth-year linebacker has been given the green light to return for Sunday's contest.

injuries.shortComment: Ridley (hip) will not practice Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Cleveland, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Ridley and Elic Ayomanor have been splitting WR snaps alongside No. 1 receiver Carnell Tate and slot man Wan'Dale Robinson. If Ridley were to miss Sunday's game, Ayomanor presumably would take on more playing time.

injuries.shortComment: The Titans opened Mausi's 21-day practice window Wednesday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official website reports.
injuries.longComment: Tennessee placed Mausi on injured reserve at the conclusion of the preseason due to a previously unspecified injury, but the team's first Week 7 injury report revealed that he's been working his way back from a foot issue. Mausi was able to turn in a full practice Wednesday, potentially giving him a shot at playing as soon as this Sunday versus the Browns if the Titans are willing to bring him back from IR.

injuries.shortComment: Winston (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Winston did not play in the Titans' Week 6 win over the Colts due to a quadriceps injury. The safety remains constrained by the injury and will need to upgrade to full participation by Friday's practice to head into Week 7 against the Browns without any injury designation.

injuries.shortComment: The Titans listed Spears as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice due to rest, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Spears had made appearances on Titans injury reports in three of the past four weeks due to ankle and knee concerns, but his absence to begin Week 7 prep was just a planned maintenance day. The fourth-year back should be ready to go for the Titans' next game against the Browns on Sunday, when he'll handle a change-of-pace role behind lead runner Tony Pollard.

injuries.shortComment: Simmons logged six tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery during the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Simmons had just 1.0 sacks through five regular-season games, but he doubled that total during Sunday's win, which was Tennessee's first of the 2026 campaign. He stripped Jonathan Taylor of the football on the Colts' opening play of the third quarter and recovered the football himself, which led to a 29-yard field goal by Joey Slye seven plays later to put the Titans on the board. Simmons leads all defensive tackles with 34 combined stops through six regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Hooker logged 13 tackles (seven solo) and one interception during the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: The Titans captured their first win of the season Sunday thanks largely to their defense and special teams. Hooker did his part with a game-high 13 combined tackles, and he made a toe-tap sideline interception off Daniel Jones late in the first quarter that stopped the Colts' red zone drive in its tracks. Hooker is up to 41 tackles (27 solo) and three pass defenses (including two interceptions) across five regular-season games and is on track to crack the tackling century mark for the first time in his eight-year NFL career.

injuries.shortComment: Helm was on the field for 33 of 46 offensive snaps (71.7 percent) but didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Helm has seen his role on offense steadily decline since his four-catch performance in Week 1 against the Jets. He's been held without a catch in each of the last two games and has seen only two targets from Cam Ward over the Titans' last three games. Tennessee's offense is one of the worst units in the league this season, and it's hard to put much stock into any of the position players outside of rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate and, to a lesser extent, veteran running back Tony Pollard. The Titans will head back home for Week 7 against the Browns on Oct. 25,

injuries.shortComment: Slye went 4-for-4 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts.
injuries.longComment: Slye was able to make multiple field goals in a contest for the second time this season and for the first time since Week 2. The kicker converted attempts from 29 and 56 yards in the third quarter before adding makes from 49 and 44 yards in the fourth. Slye now has gone 9-for-10 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, while making all seven of his extra-point tries over six contests to open the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Robinson caught three of seven targets for 22 yards during Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts.
injuries.longComment: Robinson finished tied for the team lead in targets with fellow wideout Carnell Tate, but he finished with 22 or fewer receiving yards for the second time in three weeks and the third time overall this season. The wide receiver, along with the rest of Tennessee's offense, is incredibly inconsistent, but he has seen at least five targets in four straight games.

injuries.shortComment: Tate caught six of seven targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts.
injuries.longComment: The rookie wideout capped a solid performance with an eight-yard TD in the fourth quarter, accounting for the Titans' only points on offense for the afternoon in their first win of 2026 and marking the first touchdown of his career. Tate's numbers were more remarkable considering that Cam Ward threw for a meager 102 yards in the game. Tate has begun to find a groove, posting a 22-279-1 line on 33 targets over his last four games. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 7 against the Browns.

injuries.shortComment: Pollard carried the ball 19 times for 76 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts.
injuries.longComment: Tyjae Spears had only two touches as Pollard dominated work in the Titans backfield, and the veteran RB led the team in scrimmage yards on the afternoon. Pollard's 76 rushing yards were a season high, but he's gotten into the end zone just once in six games. He'll offer a solid floor, but little ceiling, in a Week 7 matchup against the Browns.

injuries.shortComment: Ward completed 11 of 22 passes for 102 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts. He added seven yards on three carries.
injuries.longComment: The second-year QB put together his least productive game of the season, but Ward did connect with Carnell Tate for an eight-yard score in the fourth quarter. The Titans' special teams units accounted for the rest of their points in the team's first win of the year on four Joey Slye field goals and a blocked punt return for a TD. Ward has failed to reach 200 passing yards in five of six games to begin the season with a 4:4 TD:INT, giving him little fantasy appeal heading into a Week 7 tilt against the Browns.

injuries.shortComment: Adams (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Colts.
injuries.longComment: Adams exited in the first half of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. The 27-year-old has five tackles (two solo) and one pass deflection prior to exiting.

injuries.shortComment: The Titans activated Williams (pectoral) from reserve/PUP on Saturday.
injuries.longComment: The cornerback has also been cleared to play Sunday against the Colts after having his questionable tag removed. Williams will provide depth behind Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott at the position.

injuries.shortComment: Martin-Robinson (hamstring) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts.
injuries.longComment: Martin-Robinson upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited to start Week 6 prep. The tight end is all set to suit up behind Gunnar Helm and Daniel Bellinger as the No. 3 tight end for the Titans' offense while also serving on special teams.

injuries.shortComment: Flott (chest) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice session.
injuries.longComment: Flott exited the Titans' Week 5 loss to the Texans early with a chest injury. The cornerback returned to the contest briefly after sustaining the chest injury before exiting again for the remainder of the night. Despite the injury, the 25-year-old is fully back in action just a few short days after the incident.

injuries.shortComment: Ayomanor caught one of two passes for 17 yards during the Titans' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Sunday. He also added a tackle on special teams.
injuries.longComment: It was the fourth time in five games this season that Ayomanor caught one pass, with his lone connection with Cam Ward on Sunday coming late in the fourth quarter. Ayomanor was on the field for 33 of the Titans' 63 offensive snaps (52.4 percent), which was fourth-most among Tennessee wide receivers behind Carnell Tate (48), Wan'Dale Robinson (47) and Calvin Ridley (35). The Titans' 11.6 points per game is lowest in the NFL, so it's hard to put much stock into Ayomanor or any of the team's skill-position players heading into Week 6 against the Colts on Oct. 18.

injuries.shortComment: Lane underwent surgery Oct. 9 to repair his fractured and dislocated ankle, and he is expected to be cleared for activities before OTAs, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
injuries.longComment: Lane sustained his season-ending ankle injury during the Commanders' Week 4 win against the Colts, and the injury was severe enough for him to stay in London overnight to be monitored and undergo additional tests. His absence has opened the door to more playing time for both Luke McCaffrey and Dyami Brown, and they are both candidates for another bump in playing time after Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon during the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday.

injuries.shortComment: Styles finished Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers with 13 tackles (seven solo) and one pass defense.
injuries.longComment: The rookie first-rounder led the Commanders in tackles Monday, and it was his second consecutive game with 13 combined tackles. Styles is up to 46 combined tackles through six regular-season games, which leads the Commanders and ranks in the top 20 in the NFL.

injuries.shortComment: Stevens made his only field-goal try and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-17 loss at San Francisco.
injuries.longComment: The Commanders' offense put forth a mostly-uninspiring effort in Week 6, but Stevens made the most of his limited opportunities, including a 51-yard field goal to put the team on the scoreboard after its first drive of the night. Two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Terry McLaurin ruptured his patellar tendon Monday, and regular starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt went to IR with a groin injury before the game, neither of which bodes well for Washington's general offensive outlook for the coming weeks. Stevens and the Commanders will take on the Eagles in Week 8 after their bye in Week 7.

injuries.shortComment: Ekeler logged a three-yard carry and caught both of his targets for four yards during the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Despite the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Ekeler was hardly involved in the Commanders' offensive game plan. He was on the field for only seven of 67 offensive snaps, well behind Rachaad White (45) and even fewer than the returning Jeremy McNichols (12). Even with Croskey-Merritt on IR for at least the next three games, It's hard to envision a path to consistent playing time for Ekeler following the Commanders' Week 7 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Brown hauled in his only target for six yards during Monday's 23-17 loss versus San Francisco.
injuries.longComment: Despite Terry McLaurin (knee) exiting early in the loss to the 49ers, Brown wasn't on the field more than usual. He wasn't any more productive, either, catching just one pass for the second straight contest. McLaurin will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign after it was announced Tuesday that he had been diagnosed with a torn left patellar tendon. However, that doesn't mean Brown will be more involved moving forward, considering the Commanders still have Antonio Williams, Stefon Diggs and Treylon Burks in the mix.

injuries.shortComment: McNichols accrued five rushes for 13 yards during Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) sidelined, the Commanders turned to Rachaad White to do most of the heavy lifting at the running back position. McNichols, who was activated from injured reserve ahead of the Week 6 meeting with the 49ers after missing the first five games of the 2026 campaign, logged 12 offensive snaps, five more than Austin Ekeler (seven). However, neither McNichols nor Ekeler got anything going, with both players combining for six carries. With Croskey-Merritt now on injured reserve, there is room for others to step up, though it's likely White will remain the workhorse, with Ekeler and McNichols getting the leftover scraps.

injuries.shortComment: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn announced Monday that McLaurin has been diagnosed with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee following an MRI and will miss the rest of the season.
injuries.longComment: McLaurin went down with the injury on the Commanders' second possession of Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers. With McLaurin out of the mix for the rest of 2026, Stefon Diggs profiles as the Commanders' top wideout, while players such as Chig Okonkwo, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Rachaad White could see their roles in the passing game expand further. McLaurin, who is under contract with Washington through 2028, finishes the season with 230 receiving yards and a touchdown on 15 receptions over five games.

injuries.shortComment: Burks finished with four receptions for 66 yards on six targets in Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: The reception, yardage and target totals were all season-best totals for Burks, whose heightened involvement in the passing game may have been a byproduct of No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin (knee) exiting the game late in the first quarter. Though Burks didn't see a major spike in playing time compared to prior weeks -- he was on the field for 37 of 67 offensive snaps (55.2 percent) -- he should be able to maintain a regular role in three-receiver sets alongside Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, with McLaurin expected to miss time and potentially even being sidelined for the rest of the season.

injuries.shortComment: Williams brought in three of four targets for 50 yards in the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Williams finished with the third-most receptions on the Commanders for the night, and the rookie posted the second-highest receiving yardage total of his nascent career. Williams has maintained a steady complementary presence in Washington's air attack while recording at least three catches in all but one game, and the third-round pick out of Clemson should continue filling a similar role when the Commanders return from a Week 7 bye in a home divisional battle against the Eagles on Sunday night, Nov. 1. His role could increase if Terry McLaurin's knee injury ends up being serious.

injuries.shortComment: Okonkwo brought in all seven targets for 69 yards in the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: The athletic tight end set the pace for the Commanders in receptions and receiving yards while also sharing the team lead in targets. It was Okonkwo's most productive performance yet over his brief four-game Commanders tenure, and the Maryland product looks like he's hitting his stride after missing Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hamstring injury. Okonkwo will head into a Week 7 bye with a combined 11-129-0 line on 13 targets over the last two games before returning to action at home against the Eagles on Sunday night, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: White rushed seven times for 27 yards and brought in four of five targets for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) unavailable after landing on injured reserve prior to Monday's game, White worked as the de facto lead back. The ground attack took a back seat when the Commanders fell behind by a 20-3 margin going into intermission, but White was able to make an impact as a receiver. White posted his second receiving touchdown as a member of the Commanders, recording a nine-yard scoring grab in the fourth quarter for the final points of the night. With Croskey-Merritt out for at least three additional games, White could continue to see fairly solid volume in a Week 8 home matchup against the Eagles on Nov. 1 following the Commanders' Week 7 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Daniels completed 29 of 40 passes for 300 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding four rushes for 10 yards in the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Daniels' final numbers won't displease fantasy managers by any stretch, but the athletic signal-caller didn't really get the Commanders offense going until the second half. He put Washington's first touchdown of the night on the board in the waning seconds of the third quarter when he connected with Stefon Diggs from one yard out, and he followed it up with a 10-play, 90-yard march early in the fourth quarter that he capped off with a nine-yard touchdown toss to Rachaad White. However, Daniels and the Commanders came up empty on a subsequent 13-play drive that ended on downs, and the 2024 first-round pick then took a sack on the game's final play after triggering a 10-second runoff with an intentional grounding penalty on the prior snap. Despite the disappointing outcome, Daniels has been solid in his first two games back from an elbow injury, and he'll next face off with the Eagles at home on Sunday night, Nov. 1, following a Week 7 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Kinlaw (knee) won't return to Washington's matchup versus the 49ers on Monday, John Keim of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: Kinlaw is done for the night after picking up a knee injury in the first half. He had previously dealt with a shoulder issue last month. In Kinlaw's absence, Shy Tuttle and Deatrich Wise should be in line for increased playing time for the remainder of Monday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Owens (hamstring) is active for Monday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: Owens logged consecutive limited practice sessions to end Week 6 prep. The backup strong safety has not yet played a defensive snap for the Commanders this season. Owens has played 91 special-teams snaps through the first five games of the season, logging six tackles (four solo).

injuries.shortComment: Butler (hamstring) is active for Monday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: Butler returns to the lineup for the Commanders after missing the team's Week 5 tie with the Giants due to a hamstring injury. Butler will operate in his usual role as the backup at free safety to Jeremy Reaves.

injuries.shortComment: The Commanders placed Jean-Baptiste (pectoral) on injured reserve Monday.
injuries.longComment: Jean-Baptiste was already ruled out for Monday night's game against the 49ers due to a pectoral injury, which is severe enough for the third-year pro to go on IR. He's required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he is eligible to return is Week 11 against the Bengals on Monday, Nov. 23.

injuries.shortComment: The Commanders activated Magee (hamstring) from injured reserve, and he is active for Monday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: Magee has been cleared to return from a four-game absence due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 1 against the Eagles. The third-year pro is expected to work mostly on special teams, but his return bolsters the Commanders' depth at inside linebacker behind starters Frankie Luvu and rookie first-rounder Sonny Styles.

injuries.shortComment: Cross (illness) is active for Monday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: Cross was a full participant in all three practices during Week 6 prep, and the fifth-year defensive back has been cleared by medical staff to return from a three-game absence due to an internal injury. His return means Quan Martin will revert to a depth role in the secondary for Monday night's game.

injuries.shortComment: Amos (ankle) was activated from injured reserve by Washington on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Amos is active for Monday night's matchup with the 49ers, returning to action after missing the team's first five games of the season while on IR with an ankle injury. The 24-year-old will likely slot in as one of the team's starting cornerbacks against San Francisco.
